tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

def planned_dkim_name(provider: MailProvider) -> str: """Record name planned for the signing key on a fresh domain.""" return f"{provider.dkim_selectors[0] if provider.dkim_selectors else 'mail'}._domainkey" def mx_hosts(records: list[dict]) -> set[str]: return {str(r.get("data", "")).rstrip(".").lower() for r in records if r.get("type", "MX") == "MX"} """Watch an address (S10.5b): the same read-only public checks as "Check any address", once a day, for up to WATCH_LIMIT addresses per signed-in account, with one email per NEW problem. What it never does: submit forms, send email to that domain, or change anything there. It reads public DNS and opens the home page over HTTPS through the SSRF-safe fetcher (`SafeWeb`), exactly like the public tool. The only email goes to the account's own sign-in address. """ import json from datetime import timedelta from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine from sqlmodel import Session, func, select from app import audit from app.checks.dns_resolver import DnsResolver from app.checks.safe_fetch import SafeWeb from app.mail.smtp import Mailer from app.models import AuditEvent, User, WatchedAddress, utcnow WATCH_LIMIT = 3 # addresses per account ADDS_PER_DAY = 10 # adding (each add runs one check right away): rate limit per account def problems_of(results: list[dict]) -> dict[str, str]: """{check: plain sentence} for every check that failed (unknowns don't count).""" return {r["check"]: r["plain"] for r in results if r.get("ok") is False} def check_now(session: Session, w: WatchedAddress, dns: DnsResolver, web: SafeWeb) -> dict[str, str]: """Run the read-only checks for one watch and store the result. Returns the NEW problems (not seen last time).""" from app.routers.proof import address_results results = address_results(w.host, dns, web) now_bad = problems_of(results) before = set(json.loads(w.problems_json or "[]")) new = {k: v for k, v in now_bad.items() if k not in before} w.problems_json = json.dumps(sorted(now_bad)) w.results_json = json.dumps(results, ensure_ascii=False) w.last_checked_at = utcnow() session.add(w) session.commit() session.refresh(w) return new def adds_today(session: Session, user_id: int) -> int: since = utcnow() - timedelta(days=1) return session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(AuditEvent).where( AuditEvent.user_id == user_id, AuditEvent.action == "watch_added", AuditEvent.created_at >= since)).one() def alert_email(host: str, new: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]: lines = "\n".join(f" - {text}" for text in new.values()) return (f"Something changed on {host}", f"Hello,\n\nYou asked LaunchWitness to watch {host}. Today's read-only check found:\n\n{lines}\n\n" "We only read public information about that address: we didn't change anything there or contact it. " "You won't hear about these again unless they go away and come back. To stop watching it, open " "My shops in LaunchWitness and press Remove.\n\n— LaunchWitness") def run_daily(engine: Engine, mailer: Mailer, dns: DnsResolver, web: SafeWeb) -> int: """The daily job: check every watched address once; email the owner once per new problem. Returns emails sent.""" sent = 0 with Session(engine) as s: ids = s.exec(select(WatchedAddress.id)).all() for wid in ids: with Session(engine) as s: w = s.get(WatchedAddress, wid) user = s.get(User, w.user_id) if w else None if w is None or user is None or user.status not in ("pending", "approved"): continue try: new = check_now(s, w, dns, web) except Exception as e: # one bad address never stops the others audit.record(s, actor="monitor", action="watch_check", target=f"watch:{w.id}", result="failed", user_id=user.id, detail=type(e).__name__) continue if not new: continue subject, body = alert_email(w.host, new) try: mailer.send(to=user.email, subject=subject, body=body) result = "sent" sent += 1 except Exception as e: result = f"failed: {type(e).__name__}" audit.record(s, actor="monitor", action="watch_alert", target=f"watch:{w.id}", result=result.split(":")[0], user_id=user.id, detail=", ".join(sorted(new))) return sent """Watched addresses (S10.5b): a signed-in user's up-to-3 addresses, checked read-only once a day. Every route needs a signed-in user, and every query is filtered by that user: someone else's watch answers 404. """ import json from typing import Annotated from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from sqlmodel import Session, func, select from app import audit, watch from app.checks.dns_resolver import DnsResolver from app.checks.safe_fetch import SafeWeb from app.db import get_session from app.models import User, WatchedAddress from app.routers.proof import clean_address, get_public_dns, get_public_web from app.safety.access import require_user router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["watch"]) NOT_FOUND = "We couldn't find that address in your list." def out(w: WatchedAddress) -> dict: return {"id": w.id, "address": w.host, "problems": json.loads(w.problems_json or "[]"), "results": json.loads(w.results_json or "[]"), "last_checked_at": w.last_checked_at.replace(tzinfo=None).isoformat() + "Z" if w.last_checked_at else None} @router.get("/watches") def list_watches(user: Annotated[User, Depends(require_user)], session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]) -> dict: rows = session.exec(select(WatchedAddress).where(WatchedAddress.user_id == user.id) .order_by(WatchedAddress.id)).all() return {"limit": watch.WATCH_LIMIT, "watches": [out(w) for w in rows]} class AddWatch(BaseModel): address: str = Field(max_length=300) @router.post("/watches", status_code=201) def add_watch(body: AddWatch, user: Annotated[User, Depends(require_user)], session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)], dns: Annotated[DnsResolver, Depends(get_public_dns)], web: Annotated[SafeWeb, Depends(get_public_web)]) -> dict: """Add an address and check it once right away (read-only). Up to 3 per account; adds are rate-limited.""" host = clean_address(body.address) if host is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Please type a web address, like myshop.com.") mine = session.exec(select(WatchedAddress).where(WatchedAddress.user_id == user.id)).all() if any(w.host == host for w in mine): raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="You're already watching that address.") if len(mine) >= watch.WATCH_LIMIT: raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"You can watch up to {watch.WATCH_LIMIT} addresses. " "Remove one to add another.") if watch.adds_today(session, user.id) >= watch.ADDS_PER_DAY: raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail="You've added several addresses today. Please try again tomorrow.") w = WatchedAddress(user_id=user.id, host=host) session.add(w) session.commit() session.refresh(w) audit.record(session, actor="owner", action="watch_added", target=f"watch:{w.id}", result="ok", user_id=user.id, detail="read-only daily checks") # the address itself isn't written to the audit log watch.check_now(session, w, dns, web) # the first look; problems found now are shown, not emailed return out(w) @router.delete("/watches/{watch_id}") def remove_watch(watch_id: int, user: Annotated[User, Depends(require_user)], session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]) -> dict: w = session.exec(select(WatchedAddress).where(WatchedAddress.id == watch_id, WatchedAddress.user_id == user.id)).first() if w is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=NOT_FOUND) session.delete(w) session.commit() audit.record(session, actor="owner", action="watch_removed", target=f"watch:{watch_id}", result="ok", user_id=user.id) left = session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(WatchedAddress).where(WatchedAddress.user_id == user.id)).one() return {"ok": True, "left": left} """Proof routes (S9F Phase 3): the owner's "Yes, I got it", shareable read-only reports, and the public read-only "Check any address" tool.""" import secrets from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta from html import escape from typing import Annotated from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from sqlmodel import Session, func, select from app import audit, proof from app.agents.launch_check import latest_launched_plan from app.checks.dns_resolver import DnsResolver, RealDnsResolver from app.checks.safe_fetch import Refused, SafeWeb from app.config import Settings, get_settings from app.db import get_session from app.models import AddressCheck, Business, CheckRun, ReportShare, utcnow from app.routers.report import OWNER_RUNS, run_out from app.safety.access import ActorDep, require_business_access, sha, visitor_id router = APIRouter(tags=["proof"]) # ---------- "Yes, I got it" ---------- class Token(BaseModel): token: str = Field(max_length=200) @router.post("/api/proof/confirm") def confirm_test_order(body: Token, session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]) -> dict: """The button on the page the test email links to. Opening the link uses nothing up.""" t = proof.confirm(session, body.token) if t is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="This link has expired or was already used.") b = session.get(Business, t.business_id) return {"ok": True, "shop": b.name if b else ""} # ---------- shareable read-only report ---------- @router.get("/api/businesses/{business_id}/share") def share_status(b: Annotated[Business, Depends(require_business_access)], session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]) -> dict: row = active_share(session, b.id) return {"active": row is not None, "created_at": proof.iso(row.created_at) if row else None} @router.post("/api/businesses/{business_id}/share") def share_create(b: Annotated[Business, Depends(require_business_access)], actor: ActorDep, settings: Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)], session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]) -> dict: """A new link (any older one stops working). The link is shown once; only its hash is stored.""" revoke_all(session, b.id) raw = secrets.token_urlsafe(24) session.add(ReportShare(business_id=b.id, token_hash=sha(raw))) session.commit() audit.record(session, actor=actor.label, action="report_shared", target=f"business:{b.id}", result="ok", business_id=b.id, user_id=actor.user_id) return {"url": f"{settings.app_base_url.rstrip('/')}/r/{raw}"} @router.delete("/api/businesses/{business_id}/share") def share_revoke(b: Annotated[Business, Depends(require_business_access)], actor: ActorDep, session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]) -> dict: n = revoke_all(session, b.id) audit.record(session, actor=actor.label, action="report_unshared", target=f"business:{b.id}", result="ok", business_id=b.id, user_id=actor.user_id, detail=f"{n} link(s) stopped") return {"ok": True} def active_share(session: Session, business_id: int) -> ReportShare | None: return session.exec(select(ReportShare).where(ReportShare.business_id == business_id, ReportShare.revoked_at == None)).first() # noqa: E711 def revoke_all(session: Session, business_id: int) -> int: rows = session.exec(select(ReportShare).where(ReportShare.business_id == business_id, ReportShare.revoked_at == None)).all() # noqa: E711 for r in rows: r.revoked_at = utcnow() session.add(r) session.commit() return len(rows) GONE = ("" "Report not available

This report isn't available

The link may have been turned off by the shop owner.

") @router.get("/r/{token}", response_class=HTMLResponse) def shared_report(token: str, session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]): """Read-only. No customer data at all: check names, results, hop times and the servers that answered.""" row = session.exec(select(ReportShare).where(ReportShare.token_hash == sha(token[:200]))).first() b = session.get(Business, row.business_id) if row and row.revoked_at is None else None if b is None: return HTMLResponse(GONE, status_code=404) plan = latest_launched_plan(session, b.id) run_row = session.exec(select(CheckRun).where(CheckRun.business_id == b.id, CheckRun.trigger.in_(OWNER_RUNS), CheckRun.status == "done").order_by(CheckRun.id.desc())).first() run = run_out(session, run_row) if run_row and plan else None summary = proof.summary(session, run) return HTMLResponse(render_shared(b, run, summary), headers={"Cache-Control": "no-store", "X-Robots-Tag": "noindex"}) def hhmmss(iso: str | None) -> str: if not iso: return "" at = datetime.fromisoformat(iso.rstrip("Z")).replace(tzinfo=UTC) + timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30) return at.strftime("%d %b %H:%M:%S IST") def render_shared(b: Business, run: dict | None, summary: dict) -> str: practice = b.practice or any(h.get("practice") for c in (run or {}).get("checks", []) for h in c.get("hops", [])) rows = [] for c in (run or {}).get("checks", []): state = {"proven": "Proven", "needs_you": "Waiting for the owner", "failed": "Not passing"}[c["state"]] hops = " → ".join(f"{escape(h['title'])} {escape(hhmmss(h['at']))}" for h in c.get("hops", [])) rows.append(f"
  • {escape(c['title'])} · {state}" + (f"
    {hops}" if hops else "") + "
    • ") head = (f"{summary['proven']} of {summary['total']} proven" + (f", {summary['needs_you']} waiting for the owner" if summary["needs_you"] else "")) if run else \ "Not checked yet" label = "

    Practice: these results come from a " \ "pretend GoDaddy, not the real internet.

    LaunchWitness launch proof

    {escape(head)}" + (f" · last checked {escape(hhmmss(summary['last_checked_at']))}" if summary.get("last_checked_at") else "") + "

      " + "".join(rows) + "

    ") # ---------- "Check any address" (public, read-only) ---------- class Address(BaseModel): address: str = Field(max_length=300) def get_public_dns() -> DnsResolver: """FastAPI dependency: ordinary public DNS lookups (read-only). Please try again in an hour.") session.add(AddressCheck(visitor=visitor)) session.commit() return {"address": host, "read_only": True, "results": address_results(host, dns, web)} def dangling_cname(name: str, dns: DnsResolver, add) -> None: """Read-only: if `name` is a CNAME whose target doesn't exist (NXDOMAIN), say so. """Checker (code only): proves a finished launch works (SPEC §6).

Checks: site points to the server (asked of the AUTHORITATIVE nameservers via
`integ.dns`), site opens over HTTPS with a valid certificate, email settings
(MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC of the domain the order mailbox is on, compared with the
mail provider table; read-only), and a real test order arrives. Each result is
stored as a CheckResult row and an AuditEvent. Launch steps are not a check:
the report shows them separately.
"""

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import timedelta
from urllib.parse import urljoin

from sqlmodel import Session

from app import audit, proof
from app.agents.executor import Ctx
from app.agents.planner import DKIM_PENDING
from app.agents.reader import Profile
from app.mail.providers import provider_for
from app.models import CheckResult, Order, utcnow
from app.sites.orders import order_recipients


@dataclass
class Outcome:
    check: str
    passed: bool
    plain: str  # one line for the seller
    detail: str = ""  # technical
    waiting: bool = False  # passed as far as we can see, but delivery still needs the owner's "Yes, I got it"


def practice_world(ctx: Ctx) -> bool:
    return bool(ctx.integ.fake or ctx.business.practice)


def evidence(ctx: Ctx, check: str, step: str, **fields) -> None:
    proof.add(ctx.session, business=ctx.business, run_id=ctx.run_id, check=check, step=step,
              practice=practice_world(ctx), **fields)


def dns_server(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    return getattr(ctx.integ.dns, "last_server", "") or ("pretend nameserver" if ctx.integ.fake else "")


def shop_web(ctx: Ctx) -> proof.ShopWeb:
    """How the checker reaches the shop like a customer: in-process for practice, else over the internet
    to the shop's own host only (SSRF-guarded)."""
    factory = getattr(ctx.integ, "shop_web", None)
    if factory is not None:
        return factory(ctx)
    if practice_world(ctx):
        return proof.PracticeShopWeb(ctx.session, ctx.settings, ctx.integ.mailer, ctx.business, ctx.plan.site_host)
    return proof.real_shop_web(ctx.plan.site_host)


def _txt(values: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return [v.strip('"') for v in values]


def check_site_points(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    host, want = ctx.plan.site_host, ctx.settings.server_ip
    got = ctx.integ.dns.resolve(host, "A")
    ok = want in got
    evidence(ctx, "site_points", "dns_answer", answer=f"A {host} = {', '.join(got) or 'nothing'}",
             server=dns_server(ctx), source="authoritative nameserver")
    return Outcome("site_points", ok, "Your address leads to your website." if ok else
                   "Your address doesn't lead to your website yet.", f"A {host} = {got or 'nothing'}; want {want}")


HTTPS_BACKOFF = (5, 10, 20, 40, 45)  # seconds: up to 2 minutes while a new certificate is being issued


def check_https(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    url = f"https://{ctx.plan.site_host}/"
    for i in range(len(HTTPS_BACKOFF) + 1):
        r = ctx.integ.http.fetch(url)
        if r.ok and r.cert_valid:
            break
        if i < len(HTTPS_BACKOFF):
            ctx.integ.sleep(HTTPS_BACKOFF[i])
    ok = r.ok and r.cert_valid
    detail = f"status={r.status} cert_valid={r.cert_valid} {r.error}".strip()
    if not ok:
        plain = ("Your website's security certificate isn't working yet." if not r.cert_valid else
                 "Your website didn't open.")
        return Outcome("https", False, plain, detail)
    page = shop_web(ctx).get(url)
    if proof.marker(ctx.business) not in page.html:  # a parked page with a valid certificate is not her shop
        return Outcome("https", False, "Your address opens a page, but it isn't your shop.",
                       f"{detail}; shop marker missing (page status {page.status})")
    cert_end = ctx.integ.http.cert_expires(ctx.plan.site_host)
    evidence(ctx, "https", "http_response", status_code=r.status, cert_not_after=cert_end, server=page.server,
             source=url, answer="shop page with its lw-shop marker")
    return Outcome("https", True, "Your website opens securely (the padlock shows).", detail)


def mail_zone(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    """The domain whose mail settings matter for this shop's orders: the seller's own domain on
    an own-name launch, else the domain the order mailbox is on (the app's)."""
    return ctx.plan.zone if ctx.plan.mode == "full" else ctx.plan.mailbox.rsplit("@", 1)[-1].lower()


def check_email_mx(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone, provider = mail_zone(ctx), provider_for(ctx.settings)
    got = ctx.integ.dns.resolve(zone, "MX")
    hosts = {v.split()[-1].rstrip(".").lower() for v in got}
    ok = all(h in hosts for _, h in provider.mx)
    return Outcome("email_mx", ok, "Emails to your address reach your mailbox." if ok else
                   "Emails sent to your address can't reach your mailbox.",
                   f"MX {zone} = {got or 'nothing'}; expected {provider.label}")


def check_email_spf(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone, provider = mail_zone(ctx), provider_for(ctx.settings)
    got = _txt(ctx.integ.dns.resolve(zone, "TXT"))
    ok = any(v.startswith("v=spf1") and provider.spf_include in v for v in got)
    return Outcome("email_spf", ok, "Your mailbox is allowed to send email for you." if ok else
                   "Your emails may land in spam: the sending permission is missing.",
                   f"TXT {zone} = {got or 'nothing'}; expected {provider.spf_include}")


def dkim_names(ctx: Ctx, zone: str) -> list[str]:
    """Signing record names: the ones this launch planned, else whatever the live zone has."""
    names = [c["name"] for c in ctx.changes if c["name"].endswith("._domainkey")]
    if not names:
        try:
            names = sorted({r["name"] for r in ctx.integ.godaddy.get_records(zone) if r["name"].endswith("._domainkey")})
        except Exception:  # can't list the zone (not ours): fall back to the provider's usual names
            names = []
    return names or [f"{sel}._domainkey" for sel in provider_for(ctx.settings).dkim_selectors]


def check_email_dkim(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone = mail_zone(ctx)
    names, seen = dkim_names(ctx, zone), {}
    for name in names:
        txt = _txt(ctx.integ.dns.resolve(f"{name}.{zone}", "TXT"))
        seen[name] = (any(v.startswith("v=DKIM1") and "p=" in v for v in txt)
                      or bool(ctx.integ.dns.resolve(f"{name}.{zone}", "CNAME")))
    ok = bool(seen) and all(seen.values())
    return Outcome("email_dkim", ok, "Your emails are signed so customers can trust them." if ok else
                   "Your emails aren't signed, so they may land in spam.",
                   f"signing records on {zone}: {seen or 'none found'}")


def check_email_dmarc(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone = mail_zone(ctx)
    got = _txt(ctx.integ.dns.resolve(f"_dmarc.{zone}", "TXT"))
    ok = any(v.startswith("v=DMARC1") for v in got)
    return Outcome("email_dmarc", ok, "Fake emails in your name will be treated as spam." if ok else
                   "Order emails could land in spam: a protection setting is missing.",
                   f"TXT _dmarc.{zone} = {got or 'nothing'}")


TEST_CUSTOMER = {"customer_name": "LaunchWitness test", "customer_phone": "0000000000",
                 "note": "Automatic test order from your launch check. No action needed."}


def check_test_order(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    """Order from the shop like a customer: open the public page, find the order form, post it with a
    one-time test code, then record each hop separately. Delivery is proven only by finding the email in
    an inbox we can read, or by the owner tapping "Yes, I got it"; a mail server's "accepted" is not delivery."""
    url = f"https://{ctx.plan.site_host}/"
    web = shop_web(ctx)
    profile = Profile.model_validate_json(ctx.business.profile_json)
    page = web.get(url)
    form = proof.find_order_form(page.html) if page.status == 200 else None
    if form is None:
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "We couldn't open your order form for a test order.",
                       f"GET {url}: status {page.status} {page.error}".strip())
    index = next((i for i, x in enumerate(profile.products) if not x.addon), 0)
    field = f"qty_{index}"
    if field not in form.qty_fields:
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "We couldn't find an item to order on your page.", f"{field} not in form")
    ticket = proof.new_ticket(ctx.session, ctx.business, ctx.run_id)
    started = utcnow()
    fields = {**form.hidden, **TEST_CUSTOMER, field: "1", "lw_test": ticket.nonce}
    sent = web.post(urljoin(url, form.action), fields)
    ctx.session.refresh(ticket)
    order = ctx.session.get(Order, ticket.order_id) if ticket.order_id else None
    if sent.status != 200 or order is None:
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "Your order form didn't accept a test order.",
                       f"POST {form.action}: status {sent.status} {sent.error}".strip())
    evidence(ctx, "test_order", "form_post", status_code=sent.status, nonce=ticket.nonce, source=web.source,
             server=sent.server, answer=f"order {order.ref}")
    if order.email_status != "sent":
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "Your order form works, but we couldn't send the order email.",
                       f"order {order.ref}: mail server refused or unreachable")
    fake = ctx.integ.fake
    evidence(ctx, "test_order", "smtp_accepted", message_id=order.email_message_id, nonce=ticket.nonce,
             server="pretend mail server" if fake else ctx.settings.smtp_host, source="our mail server")
    recipients = [r.lower() for r in order_recipients(ctx.session, ctx.settings, ctx.business)]
    readable = fake or ctx.settings.imap_user.lower() in recipients
    if not readable:  # her own inbox: only she can prove it arrived
        return Outcome("test_order", True, "The mail server accepted a test order for you. Tap “Yes, I got it” "
                       "in that email to prove it reached your inbox.", f"order {order.ref} code {ticket.nonce}",
                       waiting=True)
    for i in range(3):
        if ctx.integ.inbox.find(subject_contains=ticket.nonce, since=started - timedelta(minutes=2)):
            evidence(ctx, "test_order", "imap_seen", nonce=ticket.nonce,
                     server="pretend inbox" if fake else ctx.settings.imap_host, source=ctx.settings.imap_user)
            return Outcome("test_order", True, "A test order reached your inbox.",
                           f"order {order.ref} code {ticket.nonce} found")
        if i < 2:
            ctx.integ.sleep(20)

                   f"order {order.ref} code {ticket.nonce} not found in {ctx.settings.imap_user}")


def check_settings_match(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    """Monitoring (daily): every setting the launch wrote still has the value it wrote."""
    current = {}
    for zone in {c["zone"] for c in ctx.changes}:
        for r in ctx.integ.godaddy.get_records(zone):
            current.setdefault((zone, r["type"], r["name"]), set()).add(str(r.get("data", "")))
    changed = []
    for c in ctx.changes:
        want = {str(r.get("data", "")) for r in c["after"]}
        have = current.get((c["zone"], c["type"], c["name"]), set())
        ok = bool(have) if (c["deferred"] or DKIM_PENDING in want) else want <= have
        if not ok:
            changed.append(f"{c['type']} {c['name']}")
    ok = not changed
    return Outcome("settings_match", ok, "Your settings are the same as at launch." if ok else
                   "Some of your settings changed since launch.", f"changed: {changed}" if changed else "all match")

    "site_points": check_site_points,
    "https": check_https,
    "email_mx": check_email_mx,
    "email_spf": check_email_spf,
    "email_dkim": check_email_dkim,
    "email_dmarc": check_email_dmarc,
    "test_order": check_test_order,
    "settings_match": check_settings_match,  # monitoring only
}
LAUNCH_CHECKS = ["site_points", "https", "email_mx", "email_spf", "email_dkim", "email_dmarc", "test_order"]
TITLES = {
    "site_points": "Your address leads to your website",
    "https": "Your website opens securely",
    "email_mx": "Emails reach your mailbox",
    "email_spf": "Your mailbox may send email for you",
    "email_dkim": "Your emails are signed",
    "email_dmarc": "Protection against fake emails in your name",
    "test_order": "A test order reached your inbox",
    "settings_match": "Your settings are unchanged since launch",
}


def checks_for(ctx: Ctx) -> list[str]:
    return list(LAUNCH_CHECKS)  # the same proof for every launch; only the allowed fixes differ by mode


def run_check(ctx: Ctx, name: str, attempt: int = 0) -> Outcome:
    try:
        out = CHECKS[name](ctx)
    except Exception as e:  # a check that crashes is a failed check, never a crash of the launch
        out = Outcome(name, False, "We couldn't complete this check.", f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300])
    save(ctx.session, ctx, out, attempt)
    return out


def save(session: Session, ctx: Ctx, out: Outcome, attempt: int) -> None:
    session.add(CheckResult(business_id=ctx.business.id, plan_id=ctx.plan.id, run_id=ctx.run_id, check=out.check, passed=out.passed,
                            detail=json.dumps({"plain": out.plain, "detail": out.detail, "waiting": out.waiting}),
                            attempt=attempt))
    if out.check.startswith("email_") and out.passed:
        evidence(ctx, out.check, "dns_answer", answer=out.detail[:200], server=dns_server(ctx),
                 source="authoritative nameserver")
    session.commit()
    audit.record(session, actor="checker", action=f"check_{out.check}", target=ctx.plan.site_host,
                 result="pass" if out.passed else "fail", business_id=ctx.business.id,
                 detail=f"attempt {attempt}: {out.detail}"[:500])


def run_all(ctx: Ctx) -> list[Outcome]:
    return [run_check(ctx, name) for name in checks_for(ctx)]
"""The ONLY repairs the Doctor may choose (SPEC §5, §9). Code applies them.

fixes make sense for which failed check in which kind of launch.

from collections.abc import Callable

from app import audit
from app.agents.executor import Ctx, StepFailed, restore_change, write_change
from app.agents.planner import DKIM_PENDING


def _changes(ctx: Ctx, pred) -> list[dict]:
    return [c for c in ctx.changes if pred(c)]


def _rewrite(ctx: Ctx, changes: list[dict]) -> str:
    if not changes:
        raise StepFailed("There's nothing in your plan to re-add for this.", "no matching planned change")
    for ch in changes:
        after = ch["after"]
        if ch["deferred"] or any(r.get("data") == DKIM_PENDING for r in after):
            _name, value = ctx.integ.mailbox.dkim(ctx.plan.zone)
            after = [{**r, "data": value} for r in after]
        write_change(ctx, ch, after)
    return f"Re-added {len(changes)} setting(s)."


def restore_backup(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    """Undo: put every setting this launch touched back as it was before."""
    for ch in ctx.changes:
        restore_change(ctx, ch)
    return "Put your settings back the way they were before the launch."


def readd_mx(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    return _rewrite(ctx, _changes(ctx, lambda c: c["type"] == "MX"))


def readd_email_auth(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    return _rewrite(ctx, _changes(ctx, lambda c: c["type"] == "TXT"))


def repoint_site(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    return _rewrite(ctx, _changes(ctx, lambda c: c["type"] == "A"))


def retry_certificate(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    """Caddy issues the certificate on demand: a fresh HTTPS request triggers a new attempt.
    TODO(real): if Caddy keeps failing, its admin API can be asked to retry (see PROGRESS.md)."""
    ctx.integ.sleep(10)
    heal = getattr(ctx.integ.http, "staged_heal", None)  # only the staged demo fault has this (launch_check.py)
    if heal is not None:
        heal()
    ctx.integ.http.fetch(f"https://{ctx.plan.site_host}/")
    return "Asked for a new security certificate."


PLAYBOOK: dict[str, Callable[[Ctx], str]] = {
    "restore_backup": restore_backup,
    "readd_mx": readd_mx,
    "readd_email_auth": readd_email_auth,
    "retry_certificate": retry_certificate,
    "repoint_site": repoint_site,
}

# Which fixes make sense for which failed check, per launch mode.
# "sandbox" = a shop on <name>.<APP_DOMAIN>: the only setting that is the shop's own is its A
# record. Mail settings there belong to the app's domain and are never written by code, and a
# missing test order has no safe automatic fix, so those checks get no fix (and no Doctor call).
# "full" = a launch on the seller's own domain (practice only for now).
FIXES_FOR: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {
    "sandbox": {
        "site_points": {"repoint_site"},
        "https": {"retry_certificate", "repoint_site"},
    },
    "full": {
        "site_points": {"repoint_site", "restore_backup"},
        "https": {"retry_certificate", "repoint_site"},
        "email_mx": {"readd_mx"},
        "email_spf": {"readd_email_auth"},
        "email_dkim": {"readd_email_auth"},
        "email_dmarc": {"readd_email_auth"},
        "test_order": {"readd_mx", "readd_email_auth"},
    },
}


def fixes_for(check: str, mode: str) -> set[str]:
    return set(FIXES_FOR.get(mode, {}).get(check, set()))


def apply_fix(ctx: Ctx, fix_id: str) -> str:
    if fix_id not in PLAYBOOK:  # callers check first; this is the last line of defence
        raise ValueError(f"{fix_id} is not in the playbook")
    message = PLAYBOOK[fix_id](ctx)
    audit.record(ctx.session, actor="doctor", action=f"fix_{fix_id}", target=ctx.plan.site_host, result="ok",
                 business_id=ctx.business.id, detail=message)
    return message

"""Checker (code only): proves a finished launch works (SPEC §6).

Checks: site points to the server (asked of the AUTHORITATIVE nameservers via
`integ.dns`), site opens over HTTPS with a valid certificate, email settings
(MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC of the domain the order mailbox is on, compared with the
mail provider table; read-only), and a real test order arrives. Each result is
stored as a CheckResult row and an AuditEvent. Launch steps are not a check:
the report shows them separately.
"""

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import timedelta
from urllib.parse import urljoin

from sqlmodel import Session

from app import audit, proof
from app.agents.executor import Ctx
from app.agents.planner import DKIM_PENDING
from app.agents.reader import Profile
from app.mail.providers import provider_for
from app.models import CheckResult, Order, utcnow
from app.sites.orders import order_recipients


@dataclass
class Outcome:
    check: str
    passed: bool
    plain: str  # one line for the seller
    detail: str = ""  # technical
    waiting: bool = False  # passed as far as we can see, but delivery still needs the owner's "Yes, I got it"


def practice_world(ctx: Ctx) -> bool:
    return bool(ctx.integ.fake or ctx.business.practice)


def evidence(ctx: Ctx, check: str, step: str, **fields) -> None:
    proof.add(ctx.session, business=ctx.business, run_id=ctx.run_id, check=check, step=step,
              practice=practice_world(ctx), **fields)


def dns_server(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    return getattr(ctx.integ.dns, "last_server", "") or ("pretend nameserver" if ctx.integ.fake else "")


def shop_web(ctx: Ctx) -> proof.ShopWeb:
    """How the checker reaches the shop like a customer: in-process for practice, else over the internet
    to the shop's own host only (SSRF-guarded)."""
    factory = getattr(ctx.integ, "shop_web", None)
    if factory is not None:
        return factory(ctx)
    if practice_world(ctx):
        return proof.PracticeShopWeb(ctx.session, ctx.settings, ctx.integ.mailer, ctx.business, ctx.plan.site_host)
    return proof.real_shop_web(ctx.plan.site_host)


def _txt(values: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return [v.strip('"') for v in values]


def check_site_points(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    host, want = ctx.plan.site_host, ctx.settings.server_ip
    got = ctx.integ.dns.resolve(host, "A")
    ok = want in got
    evidence(ctx, "site_points", "dns_answer", answer=f"A {host} = {', '.join(got) or 'nothing'}",
             server=dns_server(ctx), source="authoritative nameserver")
    return Outcome("site_points", ok, "Your address leads to your website." if ok else
                   "Your address doesn't lead to your website yet.", f"A {host} = {got or 'nothing'}; want {want}")


HTTPS_BACKOFF = (5, 10, 20, 40, 45)  # seconds: up to 2 minutes while a new certificate is being issued


def check_https(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    url = f"https://{ctx.plan.site_host}/"
    for i in range(len(HTTPS_BACKOFF) + 1):
        r = ctx.integ.http.fetch(url)
        if r.ok and r.cert_valid:
            break
        if i < len(HTTPS_BACKOFF):
            ctx.integ.sleep(HTTPS_BACKOFF[i])
    ok = r.ok and r.cert_valid
    detail = f"status={r.status} cert_valid={r.cert_valid} {r.error}".strip()
    if not ok:
        plain = ("Your website's security certificate isn't working yet." if not r.cert_valid else
                 "Your website didn't open.")
        return Outcome("https", False, plain, detail)
    page = shop_web(ctx).get(url)
    if proof.marker(ctx.business) not in page.html:  # a parked page with a valid certificate is not her shop
        return Outcome("https", False, "Your address opens a page, but it isn't your shop.",
                       f"{detail}; shop marker missing (page status {page.status})")
    cert_end = ctx.integ.http.cert_expires(ctx.plan.site_host)
    evidence(ctx, "https", "http_response", status_code=r.status, cert_not_after=cert_end, server=page.server,
             source=url, answer="shop page with its lw-shop marker")
    return Outcome("https", True, "Your website opens securely (the padlock shows).", detail)


def mail_zone(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    """The domain whose mail settings matter for this shop's orders: the seller's own domain on
    an own-name launch, else the domain the order mailbox is on (the app's)."""
    return ctx.plan.zone if ctx.plan.mode == "full" else ctx.plan.mailbox.rsplit("@", 1)[-1].lower()


def check_email_mx(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone, provider = mail_zone(ctx), provider_for(ctx.settings)
    got = ctx.integ.dns.resolve(zone, "MX")
    hosts = {v.split()[-1].rstrip(".").lower() for v in got}
    ok = all(h in hosts for _, h in provider.mx)
    return Outcome("email_mx", ok, "Emails to your address reach your mailbox." if ok else
                   "Emails sent to your address can't reach your mailbox.",
                   f"MX {zone} = {got or 'nothing'}; expected {provider.label}")


def check_email_spf(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone, provider = mail_zone(ctx), provider_for(ctx.settings)
    got = _txt(ctx.integ.dns.resolve(zone, "TXT"))
    ok = any(v.startswith("v=spf1") and provider.spf_include in v for v in got)
    return Outcome("email_spf", ok, "Your mailbox is allowed to send email for you." if ok else
                   "Your emails may land in spam: the sending permission is missing.",
                   f"TXT {zone} = {got or 'nothing'}; expected {provider.spf_include}")


def dkim_names(ctx: Ctx, zone: str) -> list[str]:
    """Signing record names: the ones this launch planned, else whatever the live zone has."""
    names = [c["name"] for c in ctx.changes if c["name"].endswith("._domainkey")]
    if not names:
        try:
            names = sorted({r["name"] for r in ctx.integ.godaddy.get_records(zone) if r["name"].endswith("._domainkey")})
        except Exception:  # can't list the zone (not ours): fall back to the provider's usual names
            names = []
    return names or [f"{sel}._domainkey" for sel in provider_for(ctx.settings).dkim_selectors]


def check_email_dkim(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone = mail_zone(ctx)
    names, seen = dkim_names(ctx, zone), {}
    for name in names:
        txt = _txt(ctx.integ.dns.resolve(f"{name}.{zone}", "TXT"))
        seen[name] = (any(v.startswith("v=DKIM1") and "p=" in v for v in txt)
                      or bool(ctx.integ.dns.resolve(f"{name}.{zone}", "CNAME")))
    ok = bool(seen) and all(seen.values())
    return Outcome("email_dkim", ok, "Your emails are signed so customers can trust them." if ok else
                   "Your emails aren't signed, so they may land in spam.",
                   f"signing records on {zone}: {seen or 'none found'}")


def check_email_dmarc(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    zone = mail_zone(ctx)
    got = _txt(ctx.integ.dns.resolve(f"_dmarc.{zone}", "TXT"))
    ok = any(v.startswith("v=DMARC1") for v in got)
    return Outcome("email_dmarc", ok, "Fake emails in your name will be treated as spam." if ok else
                   "Order emails could land in spam: a protection setting is missing.",
                   f"TXT _dmarc.{zone} = {got or 'nothing'}")


TEST_CUSTOMER = {"customer_name": "LaunchWitness test", "customer_phone": "0000000000",
                 "note": "Automatic test order from your launch check. No action needed."}


def check_test_order(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    """Order from the shop like a customer: open the public page, find the order form, post it with a
    one-time test code, then record each hop separately. Delivery is proven only by finding the email in
    an inbox we can read, or by the owner tapping "Yes, I got it"; a mail server's "accepted" is not delivery."""
    url = f"https://{ctx.plan.site_host}/"
    web = shop_web(ctx)
    profile = Profile.model_validate_json(ctx.business.profile_json)
    page = web.get(url)
    form = proof.find_order_form(page.html) if page.status == 200 else None
    if form is None:
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "We couldn't open your order form for a test order.",
                       f"GET {url}: status {page.status} {page.error}".strip())
    index = next((i for i, x in enumerate(profile.products) if not x.addon), 0)
    field = f"qty_{index}"
    if field not in form.qty_fields:
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "We couldn't find an item to order on your page.", f"{field} not in form")
    ticket = proof.new_ticket(ctx.session, ctx.business, ctx.run_id)
    started = utcnow()
    fields = {**form.hidden, **TEST_CUSTOMER, field: "1", "lw_test": ticket.nonce}
    sent = web.post(urljoin(url, form.action), fields)
    ctx.session.refresh(ticket)
    order = ctx.session.get(Order, ticket.order_id) if ticket.order_id else None
    if sent.status != 200 or order is None:
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "Your order form didn't accept a test order.",
                       f"POST {form.action}: status {sent.status} {sent.error}".strip())
    evidence(ctx, "test_order", "form_post", status_code=sent.status, nonce=ticket.nonce, source=web.source,
             server=sent.server, answer=f"order {order.ref}")
    if order.email_status != "sent":
        return Outcome("test_order", False, "Your order form works, but we couldn't send the order email.",
                       f"order {order.ref}: mail server refused or unreachable")
    fake = ctx.integ.fake
    evidence(ctx, "test_order", "smtp_accepted", message_id=order.email_message_id, nonce=ticket.nonce,
             server="pretend mail server" if fake else ctx.settings.smtp_host, source="our mail server")
    recipients = [r.lower() for r in order_recipients(ctx.session, ctx.settings, ctx.business)]
    readable = fake or ctx.settings.imap_user.lower() in recipients
    if not readable:  # her own inbox: only she can prove it arrived
        return Outcome("test_order", True, "The mail server accepted a test order for you. Tap “Yes, I got it” "
                       "in that email to prove it reached your inbox.", f"order {order.ref} code {ticket.nonce}",
                       waiting=True)
    for i in range(3):
        if ctx.integ.inbox.find(subject_contains=ticket.nonce, since=started - timedelta(minutes=2)):
            evidence(ctx, "test_order", "imap_seen", nonce=ticket.nonce,
                     server="pretend inbox" if fake else ctx.settings.imap_host, source=ctx.settings.imap_user)
            return Outcome("test_order", True, "A test order reached your inbox.",
                           f"order {order.ref} code {ticket.nonce} found")
        if i < 2:
            ctx.integ.sleep(20)
    return Outcome("test_order", False, "A test order was sent but hasn't arrived in your inbox.",
                   f"order {order.ref} code {ticket.nonce} not found in {ctx.settings.imap_user}")


def check_settings_match(ctx: Ctx) -> Outcome:
    """Monitoring (daily): every setting the launch wrote still has the value it wrote."""
    current = {}
    for zone in {c["zone"] for c in ctx.changes}:
        for r in ctx.integ.godaddy.get_records(zone):
            current.setdefault((zone, r["type"], r["name"]), set()).add(str(r.get("data", "")))
    changed = []
    for c in ctx.changes:
        want = {str(r.get("data", "")) for r in c["after"]}
        have = current.get((c["zone"], c["type"], c["name"]), set())
        ok = bool(have) if (c["deferred"] or DKIM_PENDING in want) else want <= have
        if not ok:
            changed.append(f"{c['type']} {c['name']}")
    ok = not changed
    return Outcome("settings_match", ok, "Your settings are the same as at launch." if ok else
                   "Some of your settings changed since launch.", f"changed: {changed}" if changed else "all match")


CHECKS = {
    "site_points": check_site_points,
    "https": check_https,
    "email_mx": check_email_mx,
    "email_spf": check_email_spf,
    "email_dkim": check_email_dkim,
    "email_dmarc": check_email_dmarc,
    "test_order": check_test_order,
    "settings_match": check_settings_match,  # monitoring only
}
LAUNCH_CHECKS = ["site_points", "https", "email_mx", "email_spf", "email_dkim", "email_dmarc", "test_order"]
TITLES = {
    "site_points": "Your address leads to your website",
    "https": "Your website opens securely",
    "email_mx": "Emails reach your mailbox",
    "email_spf": "Your mailbox may send email for you",
    "email_dkim": "Your emails are signed",
    "email_dmarc": "Protection against fake emails in your name",
    "test_order": "A test order reached your inbox",
    "settings_match": "Your settings are unchanged since launch",
}


def checks_for(ctx: Ctx) -> list[str]:
    return list(LAUNCH_CHECKS)  # the same proof for every launch; only the allowed fixes differ by mode


def run_check(ctx: Ctx, name: str, attempt: int = 0) -> Outcome:
    try:
        out = CHECKS[name](ctx)
    except Exception as e:  # a check that crashes is a failed check, never a crash of the launch
        out = Outcome(name, False, "We couldn't complete this check.", f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300])
    save(ctx.session, ctx, out, attempt)
    return out


def save(session: Session, ctx: Ctx, out: Outcome, attempt: int) -> None:
    session.add(CheckResult(business_id=ctx.business.id, plan_id=ctx.plan.id, run_id=ctx.run_id, check=out.check, passed=out.passed,
                            detail=json.dumps({"plain": out.plain, "detail": out.detail, "waiting": out.waiting}),
                            attempt=attempt))
    if out.check.startswith("email_") and out.passed:
        evidence(ctx, out.check, "dns_answer", answer=out.detail[:200], server=dns_server(ctx),
                 source="authoritative nameserver")
    session.commit()
    audit.record(session, actor="checker", action=f"check_{out.check}", target=ctx.plan.site_host,
                 result="pass" if out.passed else "fail", business_id=ctx.business.id,
                 detail=f"attempt {attempt}: {out.detail}"[:500])


def run_all(ctx: Ctx) -> list[Outcome]:
    return [run_check(ctx, name) for name in checks_for(ctx)]
"""The ONLY repairs the Doctor may choose (SPEC §5, §9). Code applies them.

Every fix reuses the executor's guarded writes (backup exists, domain in DB,
one type+name at a time). No fix spends money. `fixes_for(check, mode)` limits which
fixes make sense for which failed check in which kind of launch.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable

from app import audit
from app.agents.executor import Ctx, StepFailed, restore_change, write_change
from app.agents.planner import DKIM_PENDING


def _changes(ctx: Ctx, pred) -> list[dict]:
    return [c for c in ctx.changes if pred(c)]


def _rewrite(ctx: Ctx, changes: list[dict]) -> str:
    if not changes:
        raise StepFailed("There's nothing in your plan to re-add for this.", "no matching planned change")
    for ch in changes:
        after = ch["after"]
        if ch["deferred"] or any(r.get("data") == DKIM_PENDING for r in after):
            _name, value = ctx.integ.mailbox.dkim(ctx.plan.zone)
            after = [{**r, "data": value} for r in after]
        write_change(ctx, ch, after)
    return f"Re-added {len(changes)} setting(s)."


def restore_backup(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    """Undo: put every setting this launch touched back as it was before."""
    for ch in ctx.changes:
        restore_change(ctx, ch)
    return "Put your settings back the way they were before the launch."


def readd_mx(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    return _rewrite(ctx, _changes(ctx, lambda c: c["type"] == "MX"))


def readd_email_auth(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    return _rewrite(ctx, _changes(ctx, lambda c: c["type"] == "TXT"))


def repoint_site(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    return _rewrite(ctx, _changes(ctx, lambda c: c["type"] == "A"))


def retry_certificate(ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    """Caddy issues the certificate on demand: a fresh HTTPS request triggers a new attempt.
    TODO(real): if Caddy keeps failing, its admin API can be asked to retry (see PROGRESS.md)."""
    ctx.integ.sleep(10)
    heal = getattr(ctx.integ.http, "staged_heal", None)  # only the staged demo fault has this (launch_check.py)
    if heal is not None:
        heal()
    ctx.integ.http.fetch(f"https://{ctx.plan.site_host}/")
    return "Asked for a new security certificate."


PLAYBOOK: dict[str, Callable[[Ctx], str]] = {
    "restore_backup": restore_backup,
    "readd_mx": readd_mx,
    "readd_email_auth": readd_email_auth,
    "retry_certificate": retry_certificate,
    "repoint_site": repoint_site,
}

# Which fixes make sense for which failed check, per launch mode.
# "sandbox" = a shop on <name>.<APP_DOMAIN>: the only setting that is the shop's own is its A
# record. Mail settings there belong to the app's domain and are never written by code, and a
# missing test order has no safe automatic fix, so those checks get no fix (and no Doctor call).
# "full" = a launch on the seller's own domain (practice only for now).
FIXES_FOR: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {
    "sandbox": {
        "site_points": {"repoint_site"},
        "https": {"retry_certificate", "repoint_site"},
    },
    "full": {
        "site_points": {"repoint_site", "restore_backup"},
        "https": {"retry_certificate", "repoint_site"},
        "email_mx": {"readd_mx"},
        "email_spf": {"readd_email_auth"},
        "email_dkim": {"readd_email_auth"},
        "email_dmarc": {"readd_email_auth"},
        "test_order": {"readd_mx", "readd_email_auth"},
    },
}


def fixes_for(check: str, mode: str) -> set[str]:
    return set(FIXES_FOR.get(mode, {}).get(check, set()))


def apply_fix(ctx: Ctx, fix_id: str) -> str:
    if fix_id not in PLAYBOOK:  # callers check first; this is the last line of defence
        raise ValueError(f"{fix_id} is not in the playbook")
    message = PLAYBOOK[fix_id](ctx)
    audit.record(ctx.session, actor="doctor", action=f"fix_{fix_id}", target=ctx.plan.site_host, result="ok",
                 business_id=ctx.business.id, detail=message)
    return message

def resolve(self, name, rtype):
        return list(self.records.get((name, rtype), []))


class FakeWeb:
    def __init__(self):
        self.urls = []

    def get(self, url):
        self.urls.append(url)
        return Page(200, "<html></html>", url)

    def cert_not_after(self, host):
        return datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=30, hours=1)


@pytest.fixture
def checker_app(make_settings, engine, mailer, claude, integ):
    app, _ = make_app(make_settings, engine, mailer, claude, integ, address_checks_per_hour=3)
    web = FakeWeb()
    app.dependency_overrides[get_public_web] = lambda: web
    app.dependency_overrides[get_public_dns] = lambda: FakeDns({
        ("shop.example.com", "A"): ["93.184.216.34"], ("shop.example.com", "MX"): ["10 mx.example.com."],
        ("shop.example.com", "TXT"): ['"v=spf1 include:x -all"']})
    return app, web


def test_check_any_address_plain_and_read_only(checker_app, engine, mailer):
    from tests.conftest import AppClient

    app, web = checker_app
    with AppClient(app) as c:
        r = c.post("/api/check-address", json={"address": "https://Shop.Example.com/menu"})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    body = r.json()
    assert body["address"] == "shop.example.com" and body["read_only"] is True
    res = {x["check"]: x for x in body["results"]}
    assert res["address"]["ok"] and res["https"]["ok"] and res["email_mx"]["ok"] and res["email_spf"]["ok"]
    assert res["email_dmarc"]["ok"] is False and "fake emails" in res["email_dmarc"]["plain"]
    assert "30 more days" in res["certificate"]["plain"]
    assert web.urls == ["https://shop.example.com/"]
    assert mailer.sent == []  # never emails anyone
    with Session(engine) as s:
        assert len(s.exec(select(AddressCheck)).all()) == 1
        assert "shop.example.com" not in " ".join(e.model_dump_json() for e in s.exec(select(AuditEvent)).all())


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", ["10.0.0.1", "http://127.0.0.1/", "localhost", "printer.local", "", "not an address"])
def test_check_any_address_refuses_non_addresses(checker_app, bad):
    from tests.conftest import AppClient

    with AppClient(checker_app[0]) as c:
        assert c.post("/api/check-address", json={"address": bad}).status_code == 422


def test_check_any_address_is_rate_limited(checker_app):
    from tests.conftest import AppClient

    with AppClient(checker_app[0]) as c:
        codes = [c.post("/api/check-address", json={"address": "shop.example.com"}).status_code for _ in range(4)]
    assert codes == [200, 200, 200, 429]

"""S10.5b "Watch this address": up to 3 per account, read-only daily checks, one email per NEW problem."""

import pytest
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import watch
from app.models import AuditEvent, WatchedAddress
from app.routers.proof import get_public_dns, get_public_web
from tests.conftest import sign_in
from tests.test_s9_phase3_proof import FakeDns, FakeWeb

GOOD = {("shop.example.com", "A"): ["93.184.216.34"], ("shop.example.com", "MX"): ["10 mx.example.com."],
        ("shop.example.com", "TXT"): ['"v=spf1 include:x -all"'],
        ("_dmarc.shop.example.com", "TXT"): ['"v=DMARC1; p=none"']}


@pytest.fixture
def world(app):
    dns, web = FakeDns(dict(GOOD)), FakeWeb()
    app.dependency_overrides[get_public_dns] = lambda: dns
    app.dependency_overrides[get_public_web] = lambda: web
    return dns, web


@pytest.fixture
def me(client, world):
    sign_in(client, "watcher@example.org")
    return client


def test_daily_run_emails_once_per_new_problem(me, world, engine, mailer):
    dns, web = world
    me.post("/api/watches", json={"address": "shop.example.com"})
    assert watch.run_daily(engine, mailer, dns, web) == 0  # all fine: nothing sent
    del dns.records[("_dmarc.shop.example.com", "TXT")]  # a problem appears
    assert watch.run_daily(engine, mailer, dns, web) == 1
    mail = mailer.sent[-1]
    assert mail["to"] == "watcher@example.org" and "shop.example.com" in mail["subject"]
    assert "fake emails" in mail["body"] and "didn't change anything" in mail["body"]
    assert watch.run_daily(engine, mailer, dns, web) == 0  # same problem tomorrow: no repeat
    dns.records[("_dmarc.shop.example.com", "TXT")] = ['"v=DMARC1; p=none"']
    assert watch.run_daily(engine, mailer, dns, web) == 0  # fixed: quiet
    del dns.records[("_dmarc.shop.example.com", "TXT")]
    assert watch.run_daily(engine, mailer, dns, web) == 1  # came back: tell them again
    # only ever emails the watcher, never the watched domain; only reads its home page
    assert all(m["to"] == "watcher@example.org" for m in mailer.sent)
    assert set(web.urls) == {"https://shop.example.com/"}


def test_first_look_is_shown_not_emailed(me, world, engine, mailer):
    dns, web = world
    del dns.records[("_dmarc.shop.example.com", "TXT")]
    w = me.post("/api/watches", json={"address": "shop.example.com"}).json()

def mail_write_decision(ctx: Ctx, ch: dict, records: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Read the LIVE zone before writing a mail setting. "write" | "keep" (theirs is fine, skip),
    or raise: working mail of another service is never replaced (by a launch or by the Doctor)."""

    live = [r for r in ctx.integ.godaddy.get_records(ch["zone"]) if r["type"] == ch["type"] and r["name"] == ch["name"]]
    if not live:
        return "write"
    provider = provider_for(ctx.settings)
    if ch["type"] == "MX":
        if mx_hosts(live) == mx_hosts(records):
            return "keep"
        if mx_hosts(live) <= {h for _p, h in provider.mx}:
            return "write"  # ours, but incomplete
        raise StepFailed(OTHER_MAIL, f"live MX {sorted(mx_hosts(live))} is not {provider.key}")
    if ch["name"] == "@":

            raise StepFailed(OTHER_MAIL, f"live SPF {spf} does not include {provider.spf_include}")
        return "write"
    return "keep" if {str(r.get("data", "")) for r in live} != {str(r.get("data", "")) for r in records} else "write"

class DoctorRefused(Exception):
    pass


@dataclass
class Diagnosis:
    plain_explanation: str
    fix_id: str


@dataclass
class RepairResult:
    check: str
    fixed: bool
    attempts: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # [{explanation, fix_id, applied, message, passed}]
    final: Outcome | None = None
    doctor: dict | None = None  # the investigation (finding, fix_id, owner_instruction, source, trace), if there was one


def doctor_user(failed: Outcome, mode: str = "full") -> str:
    allowed = ", ".join(sorted(fixes_for(failed.check, mode))) or "(none)"
    return (f"Failed check: {failed.check}\nWhat we saw: {failed.plain}\nTechnical detail: {failed.detail}\n"
            f"Fixes allowed for this check: {allowed}")


def diagnose(claude: Claude, ctx: Ctx, failed: Outcome) -> Diagnosis:
    user = doctor_user(failed, ctx.plan.mode)
    data = claude.ask_json(fixture=f"doctor_{failed.check}", tier="cheap", system=SYSTEM, user=user,
                           schema=DIAGNOSIS_SCHEMA, max_tokens=200)
    explanation = str(data.get("plain_explanation", "")).strip()[:300]
    fix_id = str(data.get("fix_id", "")).strip()
    if fix_id not in PLAYBOOK or fix_id not in fixes_for(failed.check, ctx.plan.mode):
        audit.record(ctx.session, actor="doctor", action="diagnose", target=failed.check, result="refused",
                     business_id=ctx.business.id, detail=f"fix_id {fix_id!r} not allowed for {failed.check}")
        raise DoctorRefused(fix_id)
    audit.record(ctx.session, actor="doctor", action="diagnose", target=failed.check, result="ok",
                 business_id=ctx.business.id, detail=f"{fix_id}: {explanation}")
    return Diagnosis(explanation or failed.plain, fix_id)


def remember(ctx: Ctx, check: str, inv: Investigation) -> None:
    """Keep the finding and the trace on the failed check's own row, for the report."""
    row = ctx.session.exec(select(CheckResult).where(CheckResult.run_id == ctx.run_id, CheckResult.check == check,
                                                     CheckResult.business_id == ctx.business.id)
                           .order_by(CheckResult.id.desc())).first()
    if row is not None:
        row.doctor_json = json.dumps(inv.as_dict())
        ctx.session.add(row)
        ctx.session.commit()


def investigate_and_repair(claude: Claude, ctx: Ctx, failed: Outcome, symptom: str = "") -> RepairResult:
    """Look first (read-only), then act only through the playbook, only with a fix code allows."""
    inv = investigate(claude, ctx, failed, symptom)
    remember(ctx, failed.check, inv)
    result = RepairResult(failed.check, False, final=failed, doctor=inv.as_dict())

def doctor_user(failed: Outcome, mode: str = "full") -> str:
    allowed = ", ".join(sorted(fixes_for(failed.check, mode))) or "(none)"
    return (f"Failed check: {failed.check}\nWhat we saw: {failed.plain}\nTechnical detail: {failed.detail}\n"
            f"Fixes allowed for this check: {allowed}")


def diagnose(claude: Claude, ctx: Ctx, failed: Outcome) -> Diagnosis:
    user = doctor_user(failed, ctx.plan.mode)
    data = claude.ask_json(fixture=f"doctor_{failed.check}", tier="cheap", system=SYSTEM, user=user,
                           schema=DIAGNOSIS_SCHEMA, max_tokens=200)
    explanation = str(data.get("plain_explanation", "")).strip()[:300]
    fix_id = str(data.get("fix_id", "")).strip()
    if fix_id not in PLAYBOOK or fix_id not in fixes_for(failed.check, ctx.plan.mode):
        audit.record(ctx.session, actor="doctor", action="diagnose", target=failed.check, result="refused",
                     business_id=ctx.business.id, detail=f"fix_id {fix_id!r} not allowed for {failed.check}")
        raise DoctorRefused(fix_id)
    audit.record(ctx.session, actor="doctor", action="diagnose", target=failed.check, result="ok",
                 business_id=ctx.business.id, detail=f"{fix_id}: {explanation}")

def daily_checks(mode: str) -> list[str]:
    # The daily test order carries a fresh code. For an inbox we can't read it proves "form accepted ->
    # mail server accepted" only (the report says so); delivery needs the owner's tap on that email.
