"""The email setup of ANY domain, read from public DNS only (S11b).

Two rules run through this file:
- **Never guess.** The email service is detected from the domain's own mail-server names (one table, `SERVICES`).
  If we don't recognise it, we say so and give no values at all.
- **"Not sure" beats wrong.** Every finding says how sure we are: `seen` (we read it), `not_seen` (we looked and
  it wasn't there), `couldnt_check` (our lookup failed, or it can't be looked up at all). A lookup that failed
  on our side is never reported as something missing on theirs.

A finding is a dict: check, ok (True good / False a real problem / None a note or "not sure"), plain (no record
names or values), detail (technical), sure, code (stable id, used by tests and the matrix), steps (the
service's own instructions; we only explain, we never change anything on an outside domain).
"""

import ipaddress
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from app.checks.dns_resolver import DnsResolver, lookup, txt_value

SEEN, NOT_SEEN, COULDNT = "seen", "not_seen", "couldnt_check"
SPF_LOOKUP_LIMIT, SPF_VOID_LIMIT = 10, 2  # RFC 7208 section 4.6.4
SPF_MAX_DEPTH = 10  # nested include/redirect levels we follow
SPF_MAX_QUERIES = 30  # DNS questions one SPF walk may ask, whatever the record says


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Service:
    key: str
    label: str
    mx: tuple[str, ...]  # a mail-server name that is, or ends with, one of these belongs to this service
    spf: tuple[str, ...]  # include: targets that mean "this service may send"
    spf_line: str  # the line the service itself documents
    mx_doc: str  # the mail servers the service itself documents
    where: str  # where the owner changes it, in the service's own words
    dkim: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # documented / usual signing labels (selectors); () = it can't be looked up
    dkim_how: str = ""
    note: str = ""


# Patterns as each service documents them (checked against live DNS where docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md says so).
SERVICES: tuple[Service, ...] = (
    Service("google", "Google Workspace (Gmail)", ("google.com", "googlemail.com"), ("_spf.google.com",),
            "v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all", "smtp.google.com (priority 1)",
            "Google Admin console → Apps → Google Workspace → Gmail", ("google",),
            "In the Google Admin console open Apps → Google Workspace → Gmail → Authenticate email, create the "
            "key, add the record it shows you, then press Start authentication."),
    Service("microsoft", "Microsoft 365 (Outlook)", ("protection.outlook.com", "mx.microsoft"),
            ("spf.protection.outlook.com", "secureserver.net"),
            "v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all",
            "the one name shown for your domain in the Microsoft 365 admin center (it ends in mail.protection.outlook.com)",
            "Microsoft 365 admin center → Settings → Domains", ("selector1", "selector2"),
            "In the Microsoft Defender portal open Email & collaboration → Policies → Email authentication → DKIM, "
            "choose your domain, add the two records it shows you, then switch signing on.",
            note="Microsoft 365 bought through GoDaddy uses include:secureserver.net instead; both are accepted."),
    Service("zoho", "Zoho Mail", ("zoho.com", "zohomail.com"), ("zoho.com", "zohomail.com", "one.zoho.com"),
            "v=spf1 include:zohomail.com ~all", "mx.zoho.com (10), mx2.zoho.com (20), mx3.zoho.com (50)",
            "Zoho Mail Admin Console → Domains", ("zmail", "zoho"),
            "In the Zoho Mail Admin Console open Domains → your domain → Email Configuration → DKIM, add a "
            "selector, add the record it shows you, then press Verify."),
    Service("zoho_in", "Zoho Mail (India)", ("zoho.in", "zohomail.in"), ("zoho.in", "zohomail.in"),
            "v=spf1 include:zoho.in ~all", "mx.zoho.in (10), mx2.zoho.in (20), mx3.zoho.in (50)",
            "Zoho Mail Admin Console → Domains", ("zmail", "zoho"),
            "In the Zoho Mail Admin Console open Domains → your domain → Email Configuration → DKIM, add a "
            "selector, add the record it shows you, then press Verify."),
    Service("secureserver", "GoDaddy Professional Email", ("secureserver.net",), ("secureserver.net",),
            "v=spf1 include:secureserver.net -all", "smtp.secureserver.net (0), mailstore1.secureserver.net (10)",
            "GoDaddy → My Products → Email → your domain's DNS",
            dkim_how="GoDaddy sets up signing for Professional Email itself; ask GoDaddy support to confirm it is on."),
    Service("titan", "Titan Email", ("titan.email",), ("spf.titan.email",),
            "v=spf1 include:spf.titan.email ~all", "mx1.titan.email (10), mx2.titan.email (20)",
            "Titan's control panel → Domain verification", ("titan1",),
            "In Titan's control panel open Configure DKIM, add the record it shows you, then press Verify."),
    Service("hostinger", "Hostinger Email", ("hostinger.com", "hostinger.in"), ("_spf.mail.hostinger.com",),
            "v=spf1 include:_spf.mail.hostinger.com ~all", "mx1.hostinger.com (5), mx2.hostinger.com (10)",
            "Hostinger hPanel → Emails → your domain → DNS settings",
            ("hostingermail-a", "hostingermail-b", "hostingermail-c"),
            "In hPanel open Emails → your domain → DNS settings → Custom DKIM and add the three records it shows you."),
    Service("cloudflare", "Cloudflare Email Routing", ("mx.cloudflare.net",), ("_spf.mx.cloudflare.net",),
            "v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net ~all",
            "route1.mx.cloudflare.net, route2.mx.cloudflare.net, route3.mx.cloudflare.net",
            "Cloudflare dashboard → Email → Email Routing", ("cf2024-1",),
            "Cloudflare adds the signing record itself when Email Routing is switched on (Email → Email Routing → "
            "Settings); press \"Add records automatically\" if it is missing.",
            note="Email Routing only forwards incoming email to another inbox; it doesn't send."),
)
BY_KEY = {s.key: s for s in SERVICES}
OUR_SELECTORS = ("titan1", "mail")  # the signing labels LaunchWitness itself plans (mail/providers.py)
UNKNOWN_STEPS = ("We don't recognise the email service this address uses, so we won't guess its settings. "
                 "Ask that service for its exact values and where to enter them.")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Detected:
    key: str  # a Service key, or "null_mx" | "no_mx" | "unknown" | "mixed" | "couldnt_check"
    label: str
    service: Service | None = None
    hosts: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def mx_host(value: str) -> str:
    return value.split()[-1].rstrip(".").lower() if value.split() else ""


def service_for_host(host: str) -> Service | None:
    for s in SERVICES:
        if any(host == suffix or host.endswith("." + suffix) for suffix in s.mx):
            return s
    return None


def detect(mx_values: list[str] | tuple[str, ...]) -> Detected:
    """Which email service receives this domain's mail, from its mail-server names alone."""
    hosts = tuple(mx_host(v) for v in mx_values)
    if not hosts:
        return Detected("no_mx", "no email service")
    if all(h == "" for h in hosts):  # RFC 7505 "null MX": `0 .`
        return Detected("null_mx", "no email (switched off on purpose)")
    real = tuple(h for h in hosts if h)
    found = {s.key: s for s in (service_for_host(h) for h in real) if s is not None}
    if len(found) == 1 and all(service_for_host(h) for h in real):
        s = next(iter(found.values()))
        return Detected(s.key, s.label, s, real)
    if len(found) >= 2 or (found and len(found) < len({h for h in real})) and not all(service_for_host(h) for h in real):
        names = sorted(s.label for s in found.values()) + (["another service"] if any(
            service_for_host(h) is None for h in real) else [])
        return Detected("mixed", " and ".join(names[:2]), None, real)
    return Detected("unknown", "an email service we don't recognise", None, real)


def finding(check: str, ok: bool | None, plain: str, detail: str, sure: str, code: str, steps: str = "") -> dict:
    return {"check": check, "ok": ok, "plain": plain, "detail": detail[:600], "sure": sure, "code": code,
            "steps": steps, "action": "explain" if ok is not True and steps else "none"}


OUR_SIDE = "We couldn't read this just now (the problem was on our side, not theirs). Please try again in a few minutes."


def mail_domain(host: str, dns: DnsResolver) -> str:
    """The domain whose email settings apply to `host`: itself if it has mail servers or is a domain of its own,
    else the nearest parent that is (so a shop on shop.example.com is judged by example.com's email)."""
    zone = host.removeprefix("www.")
    own = lookup(dns, zone, "MX")
    if own.values or own.status in ("nxdomain", "error"):
        return zone
    labels = zone.split(".")
    for i in range(len(labels) - 1):
        name = ".".join(labels[i:])
        if lookup(dns, name, "NS").values:
            return name
    return zone


# ---------- mail servers (MX) ----------

def mx_finding(domain: str, dns: DnsResolver) -> tuple[dict, Detected]:
    got = lookup(dns, domain, "MX")
    if got.status == "error":
        return finding("email_mx", None, OUR_SIDE, f"MX {domain}: lookup failed", COULDNT, "mx_couldnt_check"), \
            Detected("couldnt_check", "")
    d = detect(got.values)
    detail = f"MX {domain} = {', '.join(got.values) or 'nothing'}"
    steps = mx_steps(d)
    if d.key == "no_mx":
        return finding("email_mx", False, "This address has no mail servers listed, so emails sent to it will almost "
                       "certainly not arrive.", detail, NOT_SEEN, "mx_none", steps), d
    if d.key == "null_mx":
        return finding("email_mx", False, "This address says it doesn't accept email.", detail, SEEN, "mx_null",
                       "This is a deliberate setting. If you do want email here, choose an email service and replace "
                       "this setting with the mail servers that service gives you."), d
    literal = [h for h in d.hosts if _is_ip(h)]
    if literal:
        return finding("email_mx", False, "Its mail server is listed as a bare number instead of a name, which mail "
                       "services refuse.", detail, SEEN, "mx_ip_literal", steps), d
    alias, dead, unsure = [], [], False
    for h in dict.fromkeys(d.hosts):
        if lookup(dns, h, "CNAME").values:
            alias.append(h)
            continue
        a, aaaa = lookup(dns, h, "A"), lookup(dns, h, "AAAA")
        if a.values or aaaa.values:
            continue
        if "error" in (a.status, aaaa.status):
            unsure = True
        else:
            dead.append(h)
    if dead and len(dead) == len(set(d.hosts)):
        return finding("email_mx", False, "Its mail servers are listed by names that don't exist, so emails to it "
                       "can't be delivered.", f"{detail}; no address for {', '.join(dead)}", SEEN, "mx_unresolvable",
                       steps), d
    if dead:
        return finding("email_mx", None, "One of its mail servers is listed by a name that doesn't exist. Emails "
                       "still have another way in.", f"{detail}; no address for {', '.join(dead)}", SEEN,
                       "mx_partly_unresolvable", steps), d
    if alias:
        return finding("email_mx", None, "Its mail server name is an alias for another name. The rules for email "
                       "don't allow that, and some mail services refuse it.",
                       f"{detail}; CNAME at {', '.join(alias)}", SEEN, "mx_cname", steps), d
    if d.key == "mixed":
        return finding("email_mx", None, f"Emails to this address are split between two different email services "
                       f"({d.label}), so some may go to the wrong one.", detail, SEEN, "mx_mixed", UNKNOWN_STEPS), d
    if unsure:
        return finding("email_mx", None, "It lists mail servers, but we couldn't confirm they exist just now (the "
                       "problem was on our side).", detail, COULDNT, "mx_couldnt_check"), d
    if d.key == "unknown":
        return finding("email_mx", True, "Emails to this address have somewhere to go (an email service we don't "
                       "recognise).", detail, SEEN, "mx_ok_unknown"), d
    return finding("email_mx", True, f"Emails to this address have somewhere to go: {d.label}.", detail, SEEN,
                   "mx_ok"), d


def _is_ip(text: str) -> bool:
    try:
        ipaddress.ip_address(text)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    return True


def mx_steps(d: Detected) -> str:
    if d.service is None:
        return UNKNOWN_STEPS
    return f"{d.service.label}'s own mail servers are: {d.service.mx_doc}. Set them in {d.service.where}."


# ---------- sending permission (SPF) ----------

MECH = re.compile(r"^([+\-~?]?)(all|include|a|mx|ptr|ip4|ip6|exists)(?:([:/])(.*))?$", re.I)
MODIFIER = re.compile(r"^([a-z][a-z0-9_.\-]*)=(.*)$", re.I)


def spf_records(values) -> list[str]:
    texts = [txt_value(v) for v in values]
    return [t for t in texts if t.lower() == "v=spf1" or t.lower().startswith("v=spf1 ")]


@dataclass
class SpfSeen:
    lookups: int = 0
    voids: int = 0
    queries: int = 0
    includes: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    problems: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)  # (code, technical detail)
    unsure: bool = False  # one of OUR lookups failed, or a macro we can't expand: counts are "at least"
    all: str = ""  # the qualifier of the final `all` ("+", "-", "~", "?"), "" if there is none


def spf_syntax(record: str) -> str:
    """The first term that isn't valid SPF, or ""."""
    for term in record.split()[1:]:
        m = MECH.match(term)
        if m:
            _q, name, sep, arg = m.group(1), m.group(2).lower(), m.group(3), m.group(4) or ""
            if name == "all" and sep:
                return term
            if name in ("include", "exists") and (sep != ":" or not arg):
                return term
            if name in ("ip4", "ip6"):
                try:
                    net = ipaddress.ip_network(arg, strict=False)
                except ValueError:
                    return term
                if sep != ":" or net.version != int(name[2]):
                    return term
            continue
        if not MODIFIER.match(term):
            return term
    return ""


def spf_walk(domain: str, record: str, dns: DnsResolver, seen: SpfSeen | None = None, stack: tuple[str, ...] = (),
             top: bool = True) -> SpfSeen:
    """Count the DNS lookups an SPF check of `record` costs (include, a, mx, ptr, exists, redirect), following
    includes and redirects, with a depth cap, a total-question cap and loop protection."""
    seen = seen or SpfSeen()
    stack = stack + (domain.lower(),)
    bad = spf_syntax(record)
    if bad:
        seen.problems.append(("spf_syntax", f"can't read {bad!r} in the SPF of {domain}"))
        return seen
    redirect, has_all = "", False
    for term in record.split()[1:]:
        m = MECH.match(term)
        if m is None:
            mod = MODIFIER.match(term)
            if mod and mod.group(1).lower() == "redirect":
                redirect = mod.group(2).lower().rstrip(".")
            continue
        qualifier, name, arg = m.group(1) or "+", m.group(2).lower(), (m.group(4) or "")
        if name == "all":
            has_all = True
            if top:
                seen.all = qualifier
            break  # everything after `all` is ignored
        if name in ("ip4", "ip6"):
            continue
        seen.lookups += 1
        target = (arg.split("/")[0] if m.group(3) == ":" else "").lower().rstrip(".") or domain
        if "%" in target:  # a macro: its value depends on the sender, so we can't follow it
            seen.unsure = True
            continue
        if name == "include":
            _follow(target, dns, seen, stack, "include")
        elif name in ("a", "mx"):
            _void(dns, seen, target, "A" if name == "a" else "MX")
    if redirect and not has_all:
        seen.lookups += 1
        if "%" in redirect:
            seen.unsure = True
        else:
            _follow(redirect, dns, seen, stack, "redirect", top)
    return seen


def _ask(dns: DnsResolver, seen: SpfSeen, name: str, rtype: str):
    if seen.queries >= SPF_MAX_QUERIES:
        seen.unsure = True
        return None
    seen.queries += 1
    got = lookup(dns, name, rtype)
    if got.status == "error":
        seen.unsure = True
        return None
    return got


def _void(dns: DnsResolver, seen: SpfSeen, name: str, rtype: str) -> None:
    got = _ask(dns, seen, name, rtype)
    if got is not None and not got.values:
        seen.voids += 1


def _follow(target: str, dns: DnsResolver, seen: SpfSeen, stack: tuple[str, ...], kind: str, top: bool = False) -> None:
    seen.includes.add(target)
    if target in stack:
        seen.problems.append(("spf_loop", f"{kind} of {target} goes round in a circle: {' -> '.join(stack + (target,))}"))
        return
    if len(stack) >= SPF_MAX_DEPTH:
        seen.problems.append(("spf_too_deep", f"more than {SPF_MAX_DEPTH} levels of include at {target}"))
        return
    got = _ask(dns, seen, target, "TXT")
    if got is None:
        return
    records = spf_records(got.values)
    if not got.values:
        seen.voids += 1
    if len(records) != 1:
        seen.problems.append(("spf_include_broken", f"{kind} target {target} has {len(records)} SPF records"))
        return
    spf_walk(target, records[0], dns, seen, stack, top=top and kind == "redirect")


SPF_TEXT = {
    "spf_multiple": "It has more than one sending-permission line. Mail services treat that as an error, so "
                    "neither line counts and its emails may land in spam.",
    "spf_syntax": "Its sending-permission line has a mistake in it, so mail services can't read it.",
    "spf_too_many_lookups": "Its sending-permission line makes mail services look up too many other names "
                            "({n}; the limit is 10), so they give up and treat it as broken.",
    "spf_too_many_voids": "Its sending-permission line refers to {n} names that don't exist (the limit is 2), so "
                          "mail services may treat it as broken.",
    "spf_loop": "Its sending-permission line refers back to itself in a circle, so mail services treat it as broken.",
    "spf_too_deep": "Its sending-permission line is nested too deeply to follow, so mail services treat it as broken.",
    "spf_include_broken": "Its sending-permission line refers to another name that has no working "
                          "sending-permission line of its own, so mail services treat it as broken.",
    "spf_plus_all": "Its sending-permission line allows every server in the world to send as this address, so it "
                    "protects nothing.",
    "spf_neutral_all": "Its sending-permission line takes no position on other servers, so it protects nothing.",
    "spf_no_all": "Its sending-permission line doesn't say what to do with other servers, so it protects very little.",
    "spf_missing": "It doesn't say which servers may send its email, so its emails may land in spam.",
    "spf_ok_hard": "It says which servers may send its email, and tells mail services to refuse all others.",
    "spf_ok_soft": "It says which servers may send its email, and tells mail services to treat all others as suspicious.",
    "spf_unsure": "It has a sending-permission line, but we couldn't follow everything it refers to just now, so we "
                  "can't say whether it is within the limits.",
}


def spf_steps(d: Detected, code: str) -> str:
    one = "Keep exactly one line that starts with v=spf1: merge the services you send from into it and delete the others."
    if code == "spf_multiple":
        return one
    if d.service is None:
        if d.key in ("null_mx", "no_mx"):
            return "If this address never sends email, the usual line is: v=spf1 -all"
        return UNKNOWN_STEPS
    base = f"{d.service.label}'s own line is: {d.service.spf_line}  (set it in your domain's DNS settings)."
    if code in ("spf_too_many_lookups", "spf_too_many_voids", "spf_include_broken", "spf_loop", "spf_too_deep"):
        return "Remove the services you no longer send from, so fewer names are referred to. " + base
    return base + (f" {d.service.note}" if d.service.note else "")


def spf_finding(domain: str, dns: DnsResolver, d: Detected) -> dict:
    got = lookup(dns, domain, "TXT")
    if got.status == "error":
        return finding("email_spf", None, OUR_SIDE, f"TXT {domain}: lookup failed", COULDNT, "spf_couldnt_check")
    records = spf_records(got.values)
    detail = "; ".join(records)

    def out(ok, code, sure=SEEN, extra="", **fmt):
        return finding("email_spf", ok, SPF_TEXT[code].format(**fmt), (detail + (f" ({extra})" if extra else "")),
                       sure, code, "" if ok else spf_steps(d, code))

    if not records:
        return out(False, "spf_missing", NOT_SEEN)
    if len(records) > 1:
        return out(False, "spf_multiple", extra=f"{len(records)} records")
    seen = spf_walk(domain, records[0], dns)
    counts = f"{seen.lookups} lookups, {seen.voids} empty"
    for code in ("spf_syntax", "spf_loop", "spf_too_deep"):
        hit = next((p for p in seen.problems if p[0] == code), None)
        if hit:
            return out(False, code, extra=hit[1])
    if seen.lookups > SPF_LOOKUP_LIMIT:
        return out(False, "spf_too_many_lookups", extra=counts, n=seen.lookups)
    broken = next((p for p in seen.problems if p[0] == "spf_include_broken"), None)
    if broken:
        return out(False, "spf_include_broken", extra=broken[1])
    if seen.voids > SPF_VOID_LIMIT:
        return out(False, "spf_too_many_voids", extra=counts, n=seen.voids)
    if seen.all == "+":
        return out(False, "spf_plus_all", extra=counts)
    if seen.all == "?":
        return out(False, "spf_neutral_all", extra=counts)
    if seen.unsure:
        return out(None, "spf_unsure", COULDNT, extra=f"at least {counts}")
    if seen.all == "":
        return out(None, "spf_no_all", extra=counts)
    if d.service is not None and not (seen.includes & set(d.service.spf)):
        return finding("email_spf", None, f"It has a sending-permission line, but we didn't see {d.service.label} named "
                       f"in it. If this address sends email through {d.service.label}, those emails may land in spam.",
                       f"{detail} ({counts}; expected include:{d.service.spf[0]})", NOT_SEEN, "spf_not_covering",
                       spf_steps(d, "spf_not_covering"))
    return out(True, "spf_ok_hard" if seen.all == "-" else "spf_ok_soft", extra=counts)


# ---------- protection against fake email (DMARC) ----------

DMARC_STEPS = ("Add one line at the name _dmarc under your domain. A safe start is: v=DMARC1; p=none; "
               "rua=mailto:<an address you read>. Once the reports look right, change p=none to p=quarantine.")


def dmarc_tags(record: str) -> dict[str, str] | None:
    tags = {}
    for part in record.split(";"):
        if not part.strip():
            continue
        if "=" not in part:
            return None
        k, v = part.split("=", 1)
        tags[k.strip().lower()] = v.strip()
    return tags


def dmarc_finding(domain: str, dns: DnsResolver) -> dict:
    labels = domain.split(".")
    names = [".".join(labels[i:]) for i in range(max(len(labels) - 1, 1))]  # the domain, then its parents
    for i, name in enumerate(names):
        got = lookup(dns, f"_dmarc.{name}", "TXT")
        if got.status == "error":
            return finding("email_dmarc", None, OUR_SIDE, f"TXT _dmarc.{name}: lookup failed", COULDNT,
                           "dmarc_couldnt_check")
        records = [t for t in (txt_value(v) for v in got.values) if t.lower().replace(" ", "").startswith("v=dmarc1")]
        if records:
            return _dmarc_judge(records, name, inherited=i > 0)
        if i == 0 and len(names) > 1 and not lookup(dns, names[1], "NS").values and len(labels) <= 2:
            break
    return finding("email_dmarc", False, "It isn't protected against fake emails in its name.",
                   f"TXT _dmarc.{domain} = nothing", NOT_SEEN, "dmarc_missing", DMARC_STEPS)


def _dmarc_judge(records: list[str], name: str, inherited: bool) -> dict:
    detail = f"TXT _dmarc.{name} = " + "; ".join(records)
    if len(records) > 1:
        return finding("email_dmarc", False, "It has more than one fake-email protection line, so mail services "
                       "ignore them all.", detail, SEEN, "dmarc_multiple",
                       "Keep exactly one line that starts with v=DMARC1 at _dmarc and delete the others.")
    tags = dmarc_tags(records[0])
    policy = (tags or {}).get("sp" if inherited and "sp" in (tags or {}) else "p", "").lower()
    if tags is None or tags.get("v", "").upper() != "DMARC1" or policy not in ("none", "quarantine", "reject"):
        return finding("email_dmarc", False, "Its fake-email protection line has a mistake in it, so mail services "
                       "ignore it.", detail, SEEN, "dmarc_syntax", DMARC_STEPS)
    reports = " Reports about it are sent to an address its owner chose." if tags.get("rua") else ""
    parent = " (the rule is set on its parent name)" if inherited else ""
    if policy == "none":
        return finding("email_dmarc", None, "It only watches for fake emails in its name (monitoring only): fake mail "
                       f"in its name still gets through{parent}.{reports}", detail, SEEN, "dmarc_none",
                       "When the reports look right, change p=none to p=quarantine in the line at _dmarc.")
    what = "sent to spam" if policy == "quarantine" else "refused"
    return finding("email_dmarc", True, f"It is protected against fake emails in its name: they are {what}{parent}."
                   f"{reports}", detail, SEEN, f"dmarc_{policy}")


# ---------- signing (DKIM) ----------

def selectors_for(d: Detected) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    if d.service is not None and d.service.key not in ("secureserver", "titan"):
        return d.service.dkim
    return tuple(dict.fromkeys((d.service.dkim if d.service else ()) + OUR_SELECTORS))


def dkim_finding(domain: str, dns: DnsResolver, d: Detected) -> dict:
    """A signing key can only be fetched by its label. We try the service's documented labels; anything else is
    "couldn't check", never "missing"."""
    how = d.service.dkim_how if d.service is not None else UNKNOWN_STEPS
    tried, half = [], []
    for sel in selectors_for(d):
        name = f"{sel}._domainkey.{domain}"
        tried.append(sel)
        txt = [txt_value(v) for v in lookup(dns, name, "TXT").values]
        alias = [v.rstrip(".") for v in lookup(dns, name, "CNAME").values]
        if not txt and alias:
            txt = [txt_value(v) for v in lookup(dns, alias[0], "TXT").values]
        key = next((t for t in txt if re.search(r"(^|;)\s*p=", t)), None)
        if key is not None and re.search(r"(^|;)\s*p=\s*(;|$)", key):
            return finding("email_dkim", None, "It has a signing key for its emails, but the key has been switched "
                           "off (withdrawn).", f"{name}: empty p=", SEEN, "dkim_revoked", how)
        if key is not None:
            return finding("email_dkim", True, "Its emails can be signed: we found a signing key.",
                           f"{name}: key found", SEEN, "dkim_found")
        if alias:
            half.append(f"{name} -> {alias[0]} (no key there)")
    if half:
        return finding("email_dkim", None, "Signing is set up for its emails, but the key it points to isn't "
                       "published. Signing may not be switched on yet.", "; ".join(half), NOT_SEEN, "dkim_half", how)
    tried_text = f"tried: {', '.join(tried)}" if tried else "no known label to try"
    return finding("email_dkim", None, "We couldn't check whether its emails are signed: a signing key can only be "
                   "looked up by its private label, and we don't know this address's.", tried_text, COULDNT,
                   "dkim_couldnt_check", how)


# ---------- all of it ----------

def mail_findings(host: str, dns: DnsResolver) -> list[dict]:
    domain = mail_domain(host, dns)
    mx, d = mx_finding(domain, dns)
    out = [mx, spf_finding(domain, dns, d), dkim_finding(domain, dns, d), dmarc_finding(domain, dns)]
    for f in out:
        f["domain"], f["provider"] = domain, d.key
    return out

"""What ANY website address does when a visitor types it, in plain words (S11b).

Two halves, so every case can be tested from a saved observation:
- `observe()` looks (read-only: public DNS, one secure request to the home page, one secure handshake, one plain
  http request with no body) and returns a `Seen`;
- `judge()` turns a `Seen` into findings. It only says what we saw: a status code alone never becomes "your site
  works", and something that failed on OUR side becomes "couldn't check", never a fault of theirs.

Findings have the same shape as in `mail_setup.py` (check, ok, plain, detail, sure, code, steps, action).
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from app.checks.dns_resolver import DnsResolver, lookup
from app.checks.mail_setup import COULDNT, NOT_SEEN, OUR_SIDE, SEEN, finding
from app.checks.safe_fetch import PrivateAddress, Refused, TooManyRedirects

SLOW_SECONDS = 5.0
CERT_WARN_DAYS = 14
HOST_STEPS = "Whoever hosts this website can fix this: show them this result."


@dataclass
class Seen:
    host: str
    dns: str = ""  # ok | nodata (name exists, no website address) | nxdomain | error (our lookup failed)
    ips: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    fetch: str = ""  # "" not tried | ok | timeout | refused | cert | loop | private | blocked | error
    status: int | None = None
    seconds: float = 0.0
    hsts: bool = False
    final_host: str = ""
    tls: str = ""  # "" not looked | ok | expired | not_yet_valid | wrong_host | self_signed | untrusted | bad_cert | ...
    cert_days: int | None = None
    http: str = ""  # "" not looked | redirects_https | redirects_http | serves | error | closed | timeout
    http_to: str = ""
    note: str = ""


def readable(host: str) -> str:
    """An internationalised name the way people write it (xn--mnchen-3ya.de -> münchen.de)."""
    if "xn--" not in host:
        return host
    try:
        return host.encode("ascii").decode("idna")
    except UnicodeError:
        return host


def observe(host: str, dns: DnsResolver, web, light: bool = False) -> Seen:
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit

    s = Seen(host)
    a, aaaa = lookup(dns, host, "A"), lookup(dns, host, "AAAA")
    s.ips = tuple(a.values + aaaa.values)
    s.dns = ("ok" if s.ips else "error" if "error" in (a.status, aaaa.status) else
             "nxdomain" if a.status == "nxdomain" else "nodata")
    if not s.ips:
        return s
    try:
        page = web.get(f"https://{host}/")
        s.status, s.seconds, s.hsts = page.status, round(getattr(page, "seconds", 0.0), 1), getattr(page, "hsts", False)
        s.final_host = urlsplit(page.url).hostname or host
        s.note = page.error
        s.fetch = "ok" if page.status is not None else (
            getattr(page, "kind", "") or ("cert" if not page.cert_valid else
                                          "timeout" if "imeout" in page.error or page.error == "TooSlow" else "error"))
    except TooManyRedirects:
        s.fetch = "loop"
    except PrivateAddress as e:
        s.fetch, s.note = "private", str(e)
    except Refused as e:
        s.fetch, s.note = "blocked", str(e)
    if light or s.fetch == "private":
        return s
    try:
        look = getattr(web, "tls_look", None)
        if look is not None and s.fetch != "timeout":
            t = look(host)
            s.tls, s.note = t.kind, (t.detail or s.note)
            s.cert_days = (t.not_after - datetime.now(UTC)).days if t.not_after else None
        elif look is None and s.fetch == "ok":  # an older fetcher: only the end date of a working certificate
            end = web.cert_not_after(host)
            s.tls, s.cert_days = "ok", (end - datetime.now(UTC)).days if end else None
        first = getattr(web, "http_first", None)
        if first is not None:
            s.http, s.http_to = first(host)
    except Refused as e:
        s.note = str(e)
    return s


CERT_TEXT = {
    "expired": "The security certificate has expired, so browsers show a warning instead of the site.",
    "not_yet_valid": "The security certificate isn't valid yet (its start date is in the future), so browsers show a "
                     "warning instead of the site.",
    "wrong_host": "The security certificate belongs to a different name, so browsers show a warning instead of the site.",
    "self_signed": "The security certificate was made by the site itself, not by a trusted authority, so browsers "
                   "show a warning instead of the site.",
    "untrusted": "The security certificate comes from an authority browsers don't trust, so browsers show a warning "
                 "instead of the site.",
    "bad_cert": "The security certificate didn't pass our check, so browsers are likely to show a warning instead of "
                "the site.",
}
CERT_STEPS = "Whoever hosts this website needs to install a valid certificate for exactly this name: show them this result."


def judge(s: Seen, twin: Seen | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    name, out = readable(s.host), []
    if s.dns == "error":
        return [finding("address", None, OUR_SIDE, f"A/AAAA {s.host}: lookup failed", COULDNT, "addr_couldnt_check")]
    if s.dns == "nxdomain":
        return [finding("address", False, "The address doesn't lead anywhere: this name isn't set up on the internet.",
                        f"A/AAAA {s.host}: no such name", NOT_SEEN, "addr_nxdomain",
                        "Check the spelling. If it's your name, add its website address where your domain is managed.")]
    if s.dns == "nodata":
        return [finding("address", False, "The name exists, but it doesn't lead to a website server.",
                        f"A/AAAA {s.host}: no records", NOT_SEEN, "addr_nodata",
                        "Where your domain is managed, add the website address your host gave you for this name.")]
    out.append(finding("address", True, "The address leads to a website server.", ", ".join(s.ips), SEEN, "addr_ok"))
    detail = f"https://{s.host}/ -> status {s.status} {s.note}".strip()
    cert_kind = s.tls if s.tls in CERT_TEXT else ("bad_cert" if s.fetch == "cert" else "")

                           "visitors that it is not secure.", f"{detail}; http://{s.host}/ -> {s.http_to}", SEEN,
                           "web_http_only", "Ask whoever hosts this website to switch on https (a free certificate "
                           "is enough) and to send http visitors to it."))
    elif s.fetch == "refused":
        out.append(finding("https", False, "The name leads to a server, but it didn't accept a secure connection.",
                           detail, SEEN, "web_refused", HOST_STEPS))
    elif s.fetch == "loop":
        out.append(finding("https", False, "The address keeps sending visitors on to another page without ever "
                           "arriving (too many redirects).", detail, SEEN, "web_redirect_loop", HOST_STEPS))
    elif s.fetch == "private":
        out.append(finding("https", None, s.note, detail, COULDNT, "web_private"))
    elif s.fetch == "blocked":
        out.append(finding("https", None, "The address sends visitors on to a page we don't open (not secure, or "
                           "not public), so we stopped there.", f"{detail}; {s.note}", COULDNT, "web_blocked"))
    elif s.fetch != "ok":
        out.append(finding("https", None, "We reached the server, but the answer broke off before we could read it.",
                           detail, COULDNT, "web_error"))
    else:
        out.append(_status(s, name, detail))
    if s.fetch == "ok" and s.seconds > SLOW_SECONDS:
        out.append(finding("speed", None, f"It answered, but slowly (about {round(s.seconds)} seconds). Visitors may "
                           "give up waiting.", f"{s.seconds}s", SEEN, "web_slow", HOST_STEPS))
    if s.cert_days is not None and not cert_kind:
        ok = s.cert_days >= CERT_WARN_DAYS
        out.append(finding("certificate", ok, f"The security certificate is good for {s.cert_days} more days." if ok
                           else f"The security certificate runs out in {s.cert_days} days.", f"{s.cert_days} days left",
                           SEEN, "cert_days_ok" if ok else "cert_expiring", "" if ok else
                           "Certificates normally renew themselves. Ask whoever hosts this website why this one hasn't."))
    if s.http == "redirects_https":
        out.append(finding("plain_http", True, "Visitors who type the address without https are sent to the secure "
                           "site.", f"http://{s.host}/ -> https://{s.http_to}", SEEN, "http_redirects"))
    elif s.http in ("serves", "redirects_http") and s.fetch == "ok":
        out.append(finding("plain_http", None, "The site also answers on plain http without sending visitors to the "
                           "secure version.", f"http://{s.host}/ -> {s.http} {s.http_to}", SEEN, "http_no_redirect",
                           "Ask whoever hosts this website to send http visitors to https."))
    if s.hsts:
        out.append(finding("hsts", True, "It tells browsers to always use the secure version (extra protection).",
                           "Strict-Transport-Security present", SEEN, "hsts_present"))
    if twin is not None:
        out.extend(_twin(s, twin))
    return out


def _status(s: Seen, name: str, detail: str) -> dict:
    moved = f" (after sending us on to {readable(s.final_host)})" if s.final_host and s.final_host != s.host else ""
    code = s.status or 0
    if code in (401, 403, 429):
        return finding("https", None, f"The site answered securely but turned our check away (code {code}){moved}. "
                       "It may still open for ordinary visitors.", detail, COULDNT, "web_turned_away")
    if code >= 500:
        return finding("https", False, f"The site answered securely, but with an error on its side (code {code}){moved}.",
                       detail, SEEN, "web_server_error", HOST_STEPS)
    if code >= 400:
        return finding("https", False, "The site answered securely, but its home page wasn't there "
                       f"(code {code}){moved}.", detail, SEEN, "web_client_error", HOST_STEPS)
    return finding("https", True, f"The home page answered over a secure connection (code {code}){moved}.", detail,
                   SEEN, "web_ok")


def works(s: Seen) -> bool:
    return s.fetch == "ok" and s.status is not None and s.status < 400


def _twin(s: Seen, twin: Seen) -> list[dict]:
    """The same site with and without www: say so when one opens and the other doesn't."""
    if twin.dns == "error" or twin.fetch in ("private", "blocked") or works(s) == works(twin):
        return []
    good, bad = (s, twin) if works(s) else (twin, s)
    detail = f"{good.host}: status {good.status}; {bad.host}: dns {bad.dns}, {bad.fetch or 'not tried'} {bad.status or ''}"
    if bad.dns in ("nxdomain", "nodata"):
        return [finding("www", None, f"{readable(good.host)} opens, but {readable(bad.host)} isn't set up, so visitors "
                        "who type that one won't arrive.", detail, NOT_SEEN, "www_not_set_up",
                        f"Where your domain is managed, point {readable(bad.host)} to the same place as "
                        f"{readable(good.host)}.")]
    return [finding("www", False, f"{readable(good.host)} opens, but {readable(bad.host)} doesn't, so visitors who "
                    "type that one won't arrive.", detail, SEEN, "www_disagree", HOST_STEPS)]


def twin_of(host: str, dns: DnsResolver) -> str | None:
    """The other spelling to compare: the bare name for www.x; www.x for a name that is a domain of its own."""
    if host.startswith("www."):
        return host[4:]
    return f"www.{host}" if lookup(dns, host, "NS").values else None


def web_findings(host: str, dns: DnsResolver, web) -> list[dict]:
    seen = observe(host, dns, web)
    other = twin_of(host, dns) if seen.dns == "ok" else None
    return judge(seen, observe(other, dns, web, light=True) if other else None)

Nothing here touches the network. `docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md` lists each row next to the test that proves it.
The words are written out here on purpose (not imported), so a wording change has to be made twice.

import httpx
import pytest

    "zoho": (["10 mx.zoho.com.", "20 mx2.zoho.com.", "50 mx3.zoho.com."], "zohomail.com", "~all", "zmail"),
    "zoho_in": (["10 mx.zoho.in.", "20 mx2.zoho.in.", "50 mx3.zoho.in."], "zoho.in", "~all", "zmail"),
    "secureserver": (["0 smtp.secureserver.net.", "10 mailstore1.secureserver.net."], "secureserver.net", "-all", ""),
    "titan": (["10 mx1.titan.email.", "20 mx2.titan.email."], "spf.titan.email", "~all", "titan1"),
    "hostinger": (["5 mx1.hostinger.com.", "10 mx2.hostinger.com."], "_spf.mail.hostinger.com", "~all", "hostingermail-a"),
    "cloudflare": (["10 route1.mx.cloudflare.net.", "20 route2.mx.cloudflare.net."], "_spf.mx.cloudflare.net", "~all",
                   "cf2024-1"),
}
LABELS = {"google": "Google Workspace (Gmail)", "microsoft": "Microsoft 365 (Outlook)", "zoho": "Zoho Mail",
          "zoho_in": "Zoho Mail (India)", "secureserver": "GoDaddy Professional Email", "titan": "Titan Email",
          "hostinger": "Hostinger Email", "cloudflare": "Cloudflare Email Routing"}
OUR_SIDE = "We couldn't read this just now (the problem was on our side, not theirs). Please try again in a few minutes."


def zone(provider: str | None = "google", **change) -> FakeDnsResolver:
    """A healthy domain on `provider`; `change` replaces records: key "TYPE name" → values (None removes)."""
    rec: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {(D, "A"): ["93.184.216.34"]}
    if provider:
        mx, inc, all_, sel = SETUPS[provider]
        rec[(D, "MX")] = mx
        for m in mx:
            rec[(m.split()[1].rstrip("."), "A")] = ["93.184.216.40"]
        rec[(D, "TXT")] = [f'"v=spf1 include:{inc} {all_}"']
        rec[(inc, "TXT")] = ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.0/24 -all"']
        if sel:
            rec[(f"{sel}._domainkey.{D}", "TXT")] = ['"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkq"']
        rec[(f"_dmarc.{D}", "TXT")] = ['"v=DMARC1; p=quarantine"']
    for key, values in change.items():
        rtype, name = key.split("__")
        k = (name.replace("_AT_", D).replace("__", "."), rtype)
        if values is None:
            rec.pop(k, None)
        else:
            rec[k] = values

def found(dns, host=D) -> dict[str, dict]:

    "dmarc_missing": ({"TXT___dmarc._AT_": None}, "email_dmarc", "dmarc_missing", False, "not_seen",
                      "It isn't protected against fake emails in its name."),
    "dmarc_two_lines": ({"TXT___dmarc._AT_": ['"v=DMARC1; p=none"', '"v=DMARC1; p=reject"']}, "email_dmarc",

def chain(n: int) -> dict:

class Web:
    """A fetcher that plays back one situation."""

    def __init__(self, page=None, raises=None, tls=None, http=("redirects_https", "shop.example")):
        self.page, self.raises, self.tls, self.http, self.calls = page, raises, tls, http, []

    def get(self, url):
        self.calls.append(("get", url))
        if self.raises:
            raise self.raises
        return self.page

    def tls_look(self, host):
        self.calls.append(("tls", host))
        return self.tls

    def http_first(self, host):
        self.calls.append(("http", host))
        return self.http


def page(status=200, **kw):
    from app.checks.safe_fetch import Page

    return Page(status, "", "https://shop.example/", **kw)

    assert web.calls == [("get", "https://shop.example/"), ("tls", "shop.example"), ("http", "shop.example")]
    s = ws.observe("shop.example", dns, Web(page(None, kind="cert", cert_valid=False), tls=TlsSeen("expired")))

    web = Web(page(None, kind="timeout", error="ConnectTimeout"))
    s = ws.observe("shop.example", dns, web)

def zone(provider: str | None = "google", **change) -> FakeDnsResolver:
    """A healthy domain on `provider`; `change` replaces records: key "TYPE name" → values (None removes)."""
    rec: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {(D, "A"): ["93.184.216.34"]}
    if provider:
        mx, inc, all_, sel = SETUPS[provider]
        rec[(D, "MX")] = mx
        for m in mx:
            rec[(m.split()[1].rstrip("."), "A")] = ["93.184.216.40"]
        rec[(D, "TXT")] = [f'"v=spf1 include:{inc} {all_}"']
        rec[(inc, "TXT")] = ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.0/24 -all"']
        if sel:
            rec[(f"{sel}._domainkey.{D}", "TXT")] = ['"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkq"']
        rec[(f"_dmarc.{D}", "TXT")] = ['"v=DMARC1; p=quarantine"']
    for key, values in change.items():
        rtype, name = key.split("__")
        k = (name.replace("_AT_", D).replace("__", "."), rtype)
        if values is None:
            rec.pop(k, None)
        else:
            rec[k] = values
    return FakeDnsResolver(rec)

        if key.split("_")[0] != provider.split("_")[0]:

def chain(n: int) -> dict:
    """An SPF line with n includes, each resolving to a plain record."""
    out = {"TXT___AT_": ['"v=spf1 ' + " ".join(f"include:s{i}.example" for i in range(n)) + ' -all"']}
    out.update({f"TXT__s{i}.example": ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.1 -all"'] for i in range(n)})
    return out

    assert found(zone("google", **chain(10)))["email_spf"]["code"] == "spf_not_covering"  # exactly 10 is allowed

    assert (f["code"], f["ok"], f["sure"]) == ("spf_too_many_lookups", False, "seen")
    assert f["plain"] == ("Its sending-permission line makes mail services look up too many other names (11; the "
                          "limit is 10), so they give up and treat it as broken.")
    nested = {"TXT___AT_": ['"v=spf1 include:a.example mx a ptr exists:x.example -all"'],
              "TXT__a.example": ['"v=spf1 include:b.example include:c.example a:h.example mx:h.example -all"'],
              "TXT__b.example": ['"v=spf1 redirect=d.example"'],
              "TXT__c.example": ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.2 ip6:2001:db8::/32 -all"'],
              "TXT__d.example": ['"v=spf1 include:e.example include:f.example -all"'],
              "TXT__e.example": ['"v=spf1 -all"'], "TXT__f.example": ['"v=spf1 -all"'],
              "A__h.example": ["192.0.2.3"], "MX__h.example": ["1 h.example."]}
    seen = ms.spf_walk(D, txt_value(nested["TXT___AT_"][0]), zone("google", **nested))
    # top: include, mx, a, ptr, exists = 5; a.example: 2 includes + a + mx = 4; b: redirect = 1; d: 2 includes = 2
    assert (seen.lookups, seen.all) == (12, "-")

class Web:
    """A fetcher that plays back one situation."""

    def __init__(self, page=None, raises=None, tls=None, http=("redirects_https", "shop.example")):
        self.page, self.raises, self.tls, self.http, self.calls = page, raises, tls, http, []

    def get(self, url):
        self.calls.append(("get", url))
        if self.raises:
            raise self.raises
        return self.page

    def tls_look(self, host):
        self.calls.append(("tls", host))
        return self.tls

    def http_first(self, host):
        self.calls.append(("http", host))
        return self.http

"""S11b offline matrix: every website and email case → the exact plain words, how sure we are, and whose steps.

Nothing here touches the network. `docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md` lists each row next to the test that proves it.
The words are written out here on purpose (not imported), so a wording change has to be made twice.

import ssl

import httpx
import pytest

from app.checks import mail_setup as ms
from app.checks import web_setup as ws
from app.checks.dns_resolver import FakeDnsResolver, txt_value
from app.checks.safe_fetch import PrivateAddress, Refused, SafeWeb, TlsSeen, TooManyRedirects, tls_kind

D = "shop.example"  # the domain every mail case is about

# provider -> its healthy setup: mail servers, the name its SPF line refers to, its signing label
SETUPS = {
    "google": (["1 smtp.google.com."], "_spf.google.com", "~all", "google"),
    "microsoft": (["0 shop-example.mail.protection.outlook.com."], "spf.protection.outlook.com", "-all", "selector1"),
    "zoho": (["10 mx.zoho.com.", "20 mx2.zoho.com.", "50 mx3.zoho.com."], "zohomail.com", "~all", "zmail"),
    "zoho_in": (["10 mx.zoho.in.", "20 mx2.zoho.in.", "50 mx3.zoho.in."], "zoho.in", "~all", "zmail"),
    "secureserver": (["0 smtp.secureserver.net.", "10 mailstore1.secureserver.net."], "secureserver.net", "-all", ""),
    "titan": (["10 mx1.titan.email.", "20 mx2.titan.email."], "spf.titan.email", "~all", "titan1"),
    "hostinger": (["5 mx1.hostinger.com.", "10 mx2.hostinger.com."], "_spf.mail.hostinger.com", "~all", "hostingermail-a"),
    "cloudflare": (["10 route1.mx.cloudflare.net.", "20 route2.mx.cloudflare.net."], "_spf.mx.cloudflare.net", "~all",
                   "cf2024-1"),
}
LABELS = {"google": "Google Workspace (Gmail)", "microsoft": "Microsoft 365 (Outlook)", "zoho": "Zoho Mail",
          "zoho_in": "Zoho Mail (India)", "secureserver": "GoDaddy Professional Email", "titan": "Titan Email",
          "hostinger": "Hostinger Email", "cloudflare": "Cloudflare Email Routing"}
OUR_SIDE = "We couldn't read this just now (the problem was on our side, not theirs). Please try again in a few minutes."


def zone(provider: str | None = "google", **change) -> FakeDnsResolver:
    """A healthy domain on `provider`; `change` replaces records: key "TYPE name" → values (None removes)."""
    rec: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {(D, "A"): ["93.184.216.34"]}
    if provider:
        mx, inc, all_, sel = SETUPS[provider]
        rec[(D, "MX")] = mx
        for m in mx:
            rec[(m.split()[1].rstrip("."), "A")] = ["93.184.216.40"]
        rec[(D, "TXT")] = [f'"v=spf1 include:{inc} {all_}"']
        rec[(inc, "TXT")] = ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.0/24 -all"']
        if sel:
            rec[(f"{sel}._domainkey.{D}", "TXT")] = ['"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkq"']
        rec[(f"_dmarc.{D}", "TXT")] = ['"v=DMARC1; p=quarantine"']
    for key, values in change.items():
        rtype, name = key.split("__")
        k = (name.replace("_AT_", D).replace("__", "."), rtype)
        if values is None:
            rec.pop(k, None)
        else:
            rec[k] = values
    return FakeDnsResolver(rec)


def found(dns, host=D) -> dict[str, dict]:
    return {f["check"]: f for f in ms.mail_findings(host, dns)}


def other_values(provider: str) -> list[str]:
    """Every OTHER service's own settings: none of these may ever appear in advice for `provider`."""
    out = []
    for key, (mx, inc, _all, _sel) in SETUPS.items():
        if key.split("_")[0] != provider.split("_")[0]:
            out += [inc] + [m.split()[1].rstrip(".") for m in mx]
    return [v for v in out if not (provider == "microsoft" and v == "secureserver.net")]  # GoDaddy-sold Microsoft 365


# ---------- every provider: detection, healthy, and each problem with only ITS OWN steps ----------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("provider", sorted(SETUPS))
def test_provider_is_detected_and_a_healthy_setup_is_all_good(provider):

        assert f["email_dkim"]["plain"] == "Its emails can be signed: we found a signing key."

def chain(n: int) -> dict:
    """An SPF line with n includes, each resolving to a plain record."""
    out = {"TXT___AT_": ['"v=spf1 ' + " ".join(f"include:s{i}.example" for i in range(n)) + ' -all"']}
    out.update({f"TXT__s{i}.example": ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.1 -all"'] for i in range(n)})

    assert f["plain"] == ("Its sending-permission line makes mail services look up too many other names (11; the "
                          "limit is 10), so they give up and treat it as broken.")

              "TXT__a.example": ['"v=spf1 include:b.example include:c.example a:h.example mx:h.example -all"'],
              "TXT__b.example": ['"v=spf1 redirect=d.example"'],

              "TXT__e.example": ['"v=spf1 -all"'], "TXT__f.example": ['"v=spf1 -all"'],
              "A__h.example": ["192.0.2.3"], "MX__h.example": ["1 h.example."]}
    seen = ms.spf_walk(D, txt_value(nested["TXT___AT_"][0]), zone("google", **nested))
    # top: include, mx, a, ptr, exists = 5; a.example: 2 includes + a + mx = 4; b: redirect = 1; d: 2 includes = 2
    assert (seen.lookups, seen.all) == (12, "-")

class Web:
    """A fetcher that plays back one situation."""

    def __init__(self, page=None, raises=None, tls=None, http=("redirects_https", "shop.example")):
        self.page, self.raises, self.tls, self.http, self.calls = page, raises, tls, http, []

    def get(self, url):
        self.calls.append(("get", url))
        if self.raises:
            raise self.raises
        return self.page

    def tls_look(self, host):
        self.calls.append(("tls", host))
        return self.tls

    def http_first(self, host):
        self.calls.append(("http", host))
        return self.http

def zone(provider: str | None = "google", **change) -> FakeDnsResolver:
    """A healthy domain on `provider`; `change` replaces records: key "TYPE name" → values (None removes)."""
    rec: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {(D, "A"): ["93.184.216.34"]}
    if provider:
        mx, inc, all_, sel = SETUPS[provider]
        rec[(D, "MX")] = mx
        for m in mx:
            rec[(m.split()[1].rstrip("."), "A")] = ["93.184.216.40"]
        rec[(D, "TXT")] = [f'"v=spf1 include:{inc} {all_}"']
        rec[(inc, "TXT")] = ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.0/24 -all"']
        if sel:
            rec[(f"{sel}._domainkey.{D}", "TXT")] = ['"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkq"']
        rec[(f"_dmarc.{D}", "TXT")] = ['"v=DMARC1; p=quarantine"']
    for key, values in change.items():
        rtype, name = key.split("__")
        k = (name.replace("_AT_", D).replace("__", "."), rtype)
        if values is None:
            rec.pop(k, None)
        else:
            rec[k] = values
    return FakeDnsResolver(rec)


def found(dns, host=D) -> dict[str, dict]:
    return {f["check"]: f for f in ms.mail_findings(host, dns)}


def other_values(provider: str) -> list[str]:
    """Every OTHER service's own settings: none of these may ever appear in advice for `provider`."""
    out = []
    for key, (mx, inc, _all, _sel) in SETUPS.items():
        if key.split("_")[0] != provider.split("_")[0]:
            out += [inc] + [m.split()[1].rstrip(".") for m in mx]
    return [v for v in out if not (provider == "microsoft" and v == "secureserver.net")]  # GoDaddy-sold Microsoft 365

def chain(n: int) -> dict:
    """An SPF line with n includes, each resolving to a plain record."""
    out = {"TXT___AT_": ['"v=spf1 ' + " ".join(f"include:s{i}.example" for i in range(n)) + ' -all"']}
    out.update({f"TXT__s{i}.example": ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.1 -all"'] for i in range(n)})
    return out


def test_spf_lookup_limit_counts_nested_includes():
    assert found(zone("google", **chain(10)))["email_spf"]["code"] == "spf_not_covering"  # exactly 10 is allowed
    f = found(zone("google", **chain(11)))["email_spf"]
    assert (f["code"], f["ok"], f["sure"]) == ("spf_too_many_lookups", False, "seen")
    assert f["plain"] == ("Its sending-permission line makes mail services look up too many other names (11; the "
                          "limit is 10), so they give up and treat it as broken.")
    nested = {"TXT___AT_": ['"v=spf1 include:a.example mx a ptr exists:x.example -all"'],
              "TXT__a.example": ['"v=spf1 include:b.example include:c.example a:h.example mx:h.example -all"'],
              "TXT__b.example": ['"v=spf1 redirect=d.example"'],
              "TXT__c.example": ['"v=spf1 ip4:192.0.2.2 ip6:2001:db8::/32 -all"'],
              "TXT__d.example": ['"v=spf1 include:e.example include:f.example -all"'],
              "TXT__e.example": ['"v=spf1 -all"'], "TXT__f.example": ['"v=spf1 -all"'],
              "A__h.example": ["192.0.2.3"], "MX__h.example": ["1 h.example."]}
    seen = ms.spf_walk(D, txt_value(nested["TXT___AT_"][0]), zone("google", **nested))
    # top: include, mx, a, ptr, exists = 5; a.example: 2 includes + a + mx = 4; b: redirect = 1; d: 2 includes = 2
    assert (seen.lookups, seen.all) == (12, "-")

    loop = {"TXT___AT_": ['"v=spf1 include:a.example -all"'], "TXT__a.example": ['"v=spf1 include:_AT_ -all"']}
    loop["TXT__a.example"] = [f'"v=spf1 include:{D} -all"']
    f = found(zone("google", **loop))["email_spf"]
    assert (f["code"], f["ok"]) == ("spf_loop", False)

                          "broken.")
    f = found(zone("google", TXT___AT_=['"v=spf1 include:gone.example -all"']))["email_spf"]
    assert (f["code"], f["ok"]) == ("spf_include_broken", False)

                          "line of its own, so mail services treat it as broken.")
    f = found(zone("google", TXT___AT_=['"v=spf1 a:n1.example a:n2.example mx:n3.example -all"']))["email_spf"]
    assert (f["code"], f["ok"]) == ("spf_too_many_voids", False)
    assert f["plain"] == ("Its sending-permission line refers to 3 names that don't exist (the limit is 2), so mail "
                          "services may treat it as broken.")
    deep = {"TXT___AT_": ['"v=spf1 redirect=d0.example"']}
    deep.update({f"TXT__d{i}.example": [f'"v=spf1 redirect=d{i + 1}.example"'] for i in range(40)})

    class Wildcard(FakeDnsResolver):  # like example.com: ANY label under _domainkey answers

@pytest.mark.parametrize("saw,check,code,ok,sure,plain", WEB, ids=[f"{w[1]}-{w[2]}-{i}" for i, w in enumerate(WEB)])
def test_website_matrix(saw, check, code, ok, sure, plain):
    f = {x["check"]: x for x in ws.judge(seen(**saw))}[check]
    assert (f["code"], f["ok"], f["sure"], f["plain"]) == (code, ok, sure, plain)
    assert "your site works" not in f["plain"].lower() and "93.184" not in f["plain"]

        assert f["action"] == "explain" and f["steps"]


def test_slow_is_never_called_broken_and_fast_gets_no_speed_line():
    slow = {f["check"]: f for f in ws.judge(seen(seconds=19.0))}
    assert slow["https"]["ok"] is True and slow["speed"]["ok"] is None
    assert "speed" not in {f["check"] for f in ws.judge(seen(seconds=4.9))}
    assert "hsts" not in {f["check"] for f in ws.judge(seen())}  # absent HSTS is not a finding at all

    bad = seen(host="www.shop.example", fetch="refused", status=None)

    assert (f["code"], f["ok"], f["sure"]) == ("www_disagree", False, "seen")
    assert f["plain"] == "shop.example opens, but www.shop.example doesn't, so visitors who type that one won't arrive."
    f = {x["check"]: x for x in ws.judge(seen(), seen(host="www.shop.example", dns="nxdomain", ips=(), fetch=""))}["www"]
    assert (f["code"], f["ok"], f["sure"]) == ("www_not_set_up", None, "not_seen")
    f = {x["check"]: x for x in ws.judge(seen(fetch="timeout", status=None), seen(host="www.shop.example"))}["www"]
    assert f["plain"].startswith("www.shop.example opens, but shop.example doesn't")

    assert ws.readable("xn--bcher-kva.example") == "bücher.example" and ws.readable("shop.example") == "shop.example"
    twin = seen(host="www.xn--bcher-kva.example", fetch="refused", status=None)
    f = {x["check"]: x for x in ws.judge(seen(host="xn--bcher-kva.example"), twin)}["www"]
    assert "bücher.example opens, but www.bücher.example doesn't" in f["plain"]

class Web:
    """A fetcher that plays back one situation."""

    def __init__(self, page=None, raises=None, tls=None, http=("redirects_https", "shop.example")):
        self.page, self.raises, self.tls, self.http, self.calls = page, raises, tls, http, []

    def get(self, url):
        self.calls.append(("get", url))
        if self.raises:
            raise self.raises
        return self.page

    def tls_look(self, host):
        self.calls.append(("tls", host))
        return self.tls

    def http_first(self, host):
        self.calls.append(("http", host))
        return self.http


def page(status=200, **kw):
    from app.checks.safe_fetch import Page

    return Page(status, "", "https://shop.example/", **kw)


def test_observe_reads_only_the_home_page_and_classifies_what_it_saw():
    from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

    dns = FakeDnsResolver({("shop.example", "A"): ["93.184.216.34"]})
    web = Web(page(seconds=0.31, hsts=True), tls=TlsSeen("ok", datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=30, hours=1)))
    s = ws.observe("shop.example", dns, web)
    assert (s.dns, s.fetch, s.status, s.tls, s.cert_days, s.http, s.hsts) == ("ok", "ok", 200, "ok", 30,
                                                                              "redirects_https", True)
    assert web.calls == [("get", "https://shop.example/"), ("tls", "shop.example"), ("http", "shop.example")]
    s = ws.observe("shop.example", dns, Web(page(None, kind="cert", cert_valid=False), tls=TlsSeen("expired")))
    assert (s.fetch, s.tls) == ("cert", "expired")
    web = Web(page(None, kind="timeout", error="ConnectTimeout"))
    s = ws.observe("shop.example", dns, web)
    assert s.fetch == "timeout" and ("tls", "shop.example") not in web.calls  # no second wait on a dead server
    assert ws.observe("shop.example", dns, Web(raises=TooManyRedirects("x"))).fetch == "loop"
    web = Web(raises=PrivateAddress("private"))
    assert ws.observe("shop.example", dns, web).fetch == "private" and len(web.calls) == 1
    assert ws.observe("shop.example", dns, Web(raises=Refused("no"))).fetch == "blocked"
    gone = ws.observe("nowhere.example", FakeDnsResolver({("x.example", "A"): ["1.1.1.1"]}), Web())
    assert gone.dns == "nxdomain"
    broken = FakeDnsResolver({})
    broken.errors.add("shop.example")
    assert ws.observe("shop.example", broken, Web()).dns == "error"

    dns = FakeDnsResolver({("shop.example", "A"): ["93.184.216.34"]})
    assert ws.twin_of("shop.example", dns) is None and ws.twin_of("www.shop.example", dns) == "shop.example"
    dns.set("shop.example", "NS", ["ns1.example."])
    assert ws.twin_of("shop.example", dns) == "www.shop.example"

def cert_error(code: int) -> ssl.SSLCertVerificationError:
    e = ssl.SSLCertVerificationError("certificate verify failed")
    e.verify_code = code
    return e


@pytest.mark.parametrize("error,kind", [
    (cert_error(10), "expired"), (cert_error(9), "not_yet_valid"), (cert_error(18), "self_signed"),
    (cert_error(19), "untrusted"), (cert_error(20), "untrusted"), (cert_error(62), "wrong_host"),
    (cert_error(99), "bad_cert"), (TimeoutError(), "timeout"), (ConnectionRefusedError(), "refused"),
    (ssl.SSLError("wrong version number"), "no_tls"), (OSError("unreachable"), "refused")])
def test_why_a_secure_handshake_failed(error, kind):
    assert tls_kind(error) == kind


@pytest.mark.parametrize("answer,want", [
    (httpx.Response(301, headers={"location": "https://shop.example/"}), ("redirects_https", "shop.example")),
    (httpx.Response(302, headers={"location": "http://other.example/"}), ("redirects_http", "other.example")),
    (httpx.Response(200, text="hello"), ("serves", "200")), (httpx.Response(500), ("error", "500"))])
def test_plain_http_look_is_one_pinned_request_with_nothing_followed(answer, want):
    asked = []

    def handler(request):
        asked.append((str(request.url), request.headers["host"]))
        return answer

    web = SafeWeb(lambda _h: True, resolve=lambda _h: ["93.184.216.34"], transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler))
    assert web.http_first("shop.example") == want
    assert asked == [("http://93.184.216.34/", "shop.example")]
    private = SafeWeb(lambda _h: True, resolve=lambda _h: ["10.0.0.8"], transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler))
    with pytest.raises(PrivateAddress):
        private.http_first("shop.example")
    with pytest.raises(PrivateAddress):
        private.tls_look("shop.example")


def test_safe_web_reports_time_hsts_and_timeouts():
    def handler(request):
        if request.headers["host"] == "slow.example":
            raise httpx.ReadTimeout("slow")
        return httpx.Response(200, text="ok", headers={"strict-transport-security": "max-age=600"})

    web = SafeWeb(lambda _h: True, resolve=lambda _h: ["93.184.216.34"], transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler))
    assert web.get("https://shop.example/").hsts is True
    assert web.get("https://slow.example/").kind == "timeout"

def save(kind: str, host: str, dns: RecordingDns, findings: list[dict], **more) -> None:
    if os.environ.get("LW_SAVE_FIXTURES") != "1":
        return
    FIXTURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data = {"kind": kind, "host": host, "date": date.today().isoformat(), "dns": dns.asked, **more,
            "findings": brief(findings), "plain": {f["check"]: f["plain"] for f in findings}}
    (FIXTURES / f"{kind}-{host}.json").write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

        ("neverssl.com", "no_mx"), ("jvns.ca", "unknown")]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("host,provider", MAIL)
def test_real_mail_setups(host, provider):
    dns = RecordingDns()
    findings = ms.mail_findings(host, dns)
    save("mail", host, dns, findings)
    f = {x["check"]: x for x in findings}
    assert f["email_mx"]["provider"] == provider, f["email_mx"]
    assert all(x["sure"] in ("seen", "not_seen", "couldnt_check") for x in findings)
    assert f["email_dkim"]["code"] != "dkim_missing" and "aren't signed" not in f["email_dkim"]["plain"]
    if provider in ("google", "microsoft", "zoho", "zoho_in", "secureserver", "titan"):

    from app import watch

        s.refresh(u)
        for h in hosts:

    assert len(mailer.sent) == first

# Checks matrix (S11b)

Every scenario we can meet → what we show → how sure we are → what the Doctor may do → the test that proves it.

- **Sure:** `seen` (we read it) · `not seen` (we looked, it wasn't there) · `couldn't check` (our lookup failed, or it can't be looked up).
- **Shown as:** ✓ good (`ok: true`) · ✕ a real problem (`ok: false`, the only kind that sends a "Watch this address" email) · – a note or "not sure" (`ok: null`).
- **Doctor:** *explain* = plain words plus the email service's own steps, nothing offered or applied · *fix* = a playbook fix, our shops only · *needs you* = exact plain steps for the owner.
- Tests live in `backend/tests/`. `matrix` = `test_s11b_matrix.py`, `providers` = `test_s11b_doctor_providers.py`, `network` = `test_s11b_network.py`, `gaps` = `test_s11b_gaps.py`.
- Code: `app/checks/web_setup.py` (websites), `app/checks/mail_setup.py` (email; the one provider table is `SERVICES`), `app/checks/dns_resolver.py::lookup` (every answer carries ok / no record / no such name / *our lookup failed*).

## 1. Any website ("Check any address", "Watch this address")

Outside sites are **explain only**: no fix is ever offered or applied (`matrix::test_check_any_address_only_explains`).
All rows below are proven by `matrix::test_website_matrix` unless another test is named.

| Scenario | What we show | Sure | Shown | Doctor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name doesn't exist | The address doesn't lead anywhere: this name isn't set up on the internet. | not seen | ✕ | explain |
| Name exists, no website address | The name exists, but it doesn't lead to a website server. | not seen | ✕ | explain |
| **Our** DNS lookup failed | We couldn't read this just now (the problem was on our side, not theirs)… | couldn't check | – | none |
| Resolves, nothing answers in time | The name leads to a server, but nothing answered in time. | seen | ✕ | explain |
| Resolves, secure connection refused | The name leads to a server, but it didn't accept a secure connection. | seen | ✕ | explain |
| http only, no https | This site answers only on plain http, with no padlock: browsers warn visitors that it is not secure. | seen | ✕ | explain |

| Dangling alias | Possible dangling record: … points to …, which doesn't exist. `test_s10_watchdog.py` | seen | ✕ | explain |

the same private-network guard: `matrix::test_plain_http_look_is_one_pinned_request_with_nothing_followed`.

**Our own shops** keep the stricter rule: the page must carry the shop's `lw-shop` marker, so a parked or wrong page fails

| Hostinger Email | `hostinger.com`, `hostinger.in` | `_spf.mail.hostinger.com` | `hostingermail-a/b/c` | **no**: from memory of Hostinger's docs |
| Cloudflare Email Routing | `mx.cloudflare.net` | `_spf.mx.cloudflare.net` | `cf2024-1` | **no**: from memory of Cloudflare's docs |

**Bugs the real run found (each got a failing offline test first, then the fix):**

# Checks matrix (S11b)

Every scenario we can meet → what we show → how sure we are → what the Doctor may do → the test that proves it.

- **Sure:** `seen` (we read it) · `not seen` (we looked, it wasn't there) · `couldn't check` (our lookup failed, or it can't be looked up).
- **Shown as:** ✓ good (`ok: true`) · ✕ a real problem (`ok: false`, the only kind that sends a "Watch this address" email) · – a note or "not sure" (`ok: null`).
- **Doctor:** *explain* = plain words plus the email service's own steps, nothing offered or applied · *fix* = a playbook fix, our shops only · *needs you* = exact plain steps for the owner.
- Tests live in `backend/tests/`. `matrix` = `test_s11b_matrix.py`, `providers` = `test_s11b_doctor_providers.py`, `network` = `test_s11b_network.py`, `gaps` = `test_s11b_gaps.py`.

| untrusted-root.badssl.com | certificate from an authority browsers don't trust |

| neverssl.com (web) | answers only on plain http; www opens but the bare name doesn't |

| example.com (web) | answered securely (200) · certificate good · also answers on plain http with no redirect (a note) |

offline only.

**Bugs the real run found (each got a failing offline test first, then the fix):**
1. Zoho's own SPF names (`spf.zoho.com`, `spf.zohomail.com`) weren't recognised as Zoho → "didn't see Zoho named". Names under a service's name now count.
2. example.com answers for *any* signing label (a wildcard), so we said "it has a signing key, switched off". Now: a wildcard → couldn't check; a domain with no email → "no signing to check"; an unknown service → no labels tried.
3. A blog subdomain that is an alias was judged as its own email domain. An alias is no longer treated as a domain.
4. example.com: the page opened, yet we said "certificate not trusted", because the handshake used the system's trust list and the fetch used another. Both now use the same list, and a page that opened is never called a certificate failure.
5. expired.badssl.com came out as "untrusted" for the same reason; now "expired".
6. http.badssl.com (https redirects to http) came out as a vague "page we don't open". Now its own finding.
7. Old test fixtures had a mail server with no address and an SPF line referring to a name with no SPF; both are now (correctly) reported, so the fixtures were made genuinely healthy.

github.com. First run: one alert email, to the watcher only; second run: none. Nothing is sent to the watched domains.

## 3. Our own shops: the Doctor

| Scenario | What happens | Test |
|---|---|---|
| The seller's email is on another service (Google, Microsoft, Zoho, Zoho India, Titan, Hostinger, Cloudflare, unknown) and an email check fails | **Needs you**, written by code (the model isn't asked): "Email for your address is now handled by *Service*… we never change another email service's settings", plus that service's own steps. Nothing is written. | `providers::test_another_services_mail_is_explained_never_fixed_or_overwritten` (8 services × 2 checks) |
| The same, and a fix is asked for directly | The guarded write refuses; the zone is unchanged. | same |
| Our own mail servers went missing | **Fix** (`readd_mx`), re-checked. | `providers::test_our_own_missing_settings_are_still_fixed` |
| Her SPF line names us and another sender; she added a record after launch | Both are kept. | `providers::test_a_shared_spf_line_and_later_records_are_kept` |
| Mail sign-in refused | The instruction is the code's (`MAIL_SIGN_IN_REFUSED`), never the model's. | `test_s11_doctor.py` |

## 4. Real-network run (2026-11-16, from the owner's laptop)

Read-only: public DNS questions and one home-page visit each. How to run: `cd backend && ../.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -m network tests/test_s11b_network.py -q`
(add `LW_SAVE_FIXTURES=1` to re-save `tests/fixtures/network/*.json`; email addresses in the saved answers are replaced). The saved answers are
replayed offline by `matrix::test_saved_real_answers_still_give_the_same_findings` (17 files).

| Domain | What we showed |
|---|---|
| google.com | Google Workspace · SPF good (`~all`) · signing: couldn't check (label unknown) · fake-email protection: refused |
| microsoft.com | Microsoft 365 · SPF good (`-all`, 6 lookups) · signing key found (`selector2`) · refused |
| zoho.com / zoho.in | Zoho Mail / Zoho Mail (India) · SPF good · signing: couldn't check · refused |
| launchwitness.com | GoDaddy Professional Email · SPF good (`-all`) · signing: couldn't check · sent to spam |
| titan.email | Titan Email · SPF good (7 lookups) · signing key found (`titan1`) · refused |
| example.com (mail) | says it doesn't accept email · SPF good (`-all`) · no signing to check · refused |
| neverssl.com (mail) | no mail servers · SPF missing · no signing to check · protection missing |
| jvns.ca | an email service we don't recognise · SPF `?all` (protects nothing) · couldn't check · sent to spam; steps give no values |
| expired.badssl.com | certificate expired |
| wrong.host.badssl.com | certificate belongs to a different name |
| self-signed.badssl.com | certificate made by the site itself |
| untrusted-root.badssl.com | certificate from an authority browsers don't trust |
| http.badssl.com | the secure address sends visitors back to plain http |
| neverssl.com (web) | answers only on plain http; www opens but the bare name doesn't |
| github.com | answered securely (200) · certificate good · http → https · HSTS |
| example.com (web) | answered securely (200) · certificate good · also answers on plain http with no redirect (a note) |

Not found: a domain on Cloudflare Email Routing or Hostinger Email that I could identify from public DNS alone, so those two rows are proven
offline only.

**Bugs the real run found (each got a failing offline test first, then the fix):**
1. Zoho's own SPF names (`spf.zoho.com`, `spf.zohomail.com`) weren't recognised as Zoho → "didn't see Zoho named". Names under a service's name now count.
2. example.com answers for *any* signing label (a wildcard), so we said "it has a signing key, switched off". Now: a wildcard → couldn't check; a domain with no email → "no signing to check"; an unknown service → no labels tried.
3. A blog subdomain that is an alias was judged as its own email domain. An alias is no longer treated as a domain.
4. example.com: the page opened, yet we said "certificate not trusted", because the handshake used the system's trust list and the fetch used another. Both now use the same list, and a page that opened is never called a certificate failure.
5. expired.badssl.com came out as "untrusted" for the same reason; now "expired".
6. http.badssl.com (https redirects to http) came out as a vague "page we don't open". Now its own finding.
7. Old test fixtures had a mail server with no address and an SPF line referring to a name with no SPF; both are now (correctly) reported, so the fixtures were made genuinely healthy.

**Watch job on real addresses** (`network::test_watch_job_on_real_addresses_is_read_only_and_does_not_repeat`): example.com, expired.badssl.com,
github.com. First run: one alert email, to the watcher only; second run: none. Nothing is sent to the watched domains.

from tests.test_m4_report import alerts, full_launch, set_email

SHOP = "meera.launchwitness.com"


class ClaudeDown:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = 0

    def ask_json(self, **_kw):
        self.calls += 1
        raise ClaudeUnavailable("down")

    live = ask_json


@pytest.fixture
def monitor(engine, settings, integ, claude):
    return Monitor(engine, settings, lambda _b: integ, claude)


def last_run(engine) -> CheckRun:
    with Session(engine) as s:

def plan_id(engine, business_id: int) -> int:
